ghoratapena.meaning_2: terrible austerity; dreadful ascetic practice; awful self-mortification
ghoratapena.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a compound adjective formed from 'ghora' (terrible/awful) and 'tapa' (austerity/ascetic practice). The word describes an extreme or dreadful form of ascetic practice, likely referring to severe self-mortification practices mentioned in various Indian ascetic traditions.

bhuñjitabbakaṃ.meaning_2: should be eaten; can be eaten; edible; lit. to be eaten
bhuñjitabbakaṃ.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] The word appears to be a potential participle form with an added suffix '-ka', possibly functioning as a noun meaning 'that which should be eaten' or 'edible thing'. The '-ka' suffix may serve to nominalize the participle, creating a substantive meaning 'the edible portion' or 'what is to be consumed'.

abhihaṭamattameva.meaning_2: merely offered food; just the pre-arranged meal; only what has been brought
abhihaṭamattameva.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a sandhi compound combining 'abhihaṭa' (offered food, brought) with 'matta' (mere, just). The context suggests it refers to simple, pre-arranged food offerings without special preparation or ceremony. The final 'eva' emphasizes the exclusivity: 'only the offered food' or 'merely what has been brought'.

daṇḍādīhi.meaning_2: stick and so on; punishment etc.; beginning with stick
daṇḍādīhi.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] The word 'daṇḍādīhi' appears to be the instrumental plural of a compound meaning 'beginning with stick' or 'stick and so forth'. In context, it likely refers to various forms of punishment or disciplinary measures (daṇḍa meaning punishment/penalty) along with other similar measures.

khīrasadisaṃ.meaning_2: like milk; resembling milk; similar to milk
khīrasadisaṃ.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a kammadhāraya compound where 'khīra' (milk) functions as the upamāna (standard of comparison) and 'sadisa' (similar) indicates resemblance. The compound describes something that has the qualities or appearance of milk.

duyhamānameva.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a present passive participle form meaning 'being milked'. The word appears to be in the masculine nominative singular form, functioning as a verbal adjective describing the state of being milked.

khañjappahārena.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a compound noun consisting of 'khañja' (lame/limping) + 'pahāra' (blow/strike). The context suggests this refers to an ineffective or poorly executed blow, perhaps one delivered while off-balance or with impaired movement.

laddhasampattiṃ.meaning_2: obtained prosperity; acquired wealth; gained success
laddhasampattiṃ.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a sandhi compound formed from the past participle 'laddha' (obtained) and the feminine abstract noun 'sampatti' (prosperity, success). The compound literally means 'obtained prosperity' or 'acquired wealth', suggesting material or spiritual gains that have been successfully attained.

paññāyetaṃ.meaning_2: is evident; is clearly known; is perceived; there is
paññāyetaṃ.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] The form paññāyetaṃ is a passive present 3rd person singular with the enclitic pronoun etaṃ ('this') attached. It literally means 'this is known' but functions idiomatically as 'this is evident' or 'there is' in the context.

viddhaṃsayamānaṃ.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] The word appears to be a present participle form of viddhaṃsati (to fall away, drop down) with the -māna suffix, indicating an ongoing action of falling away or collapsing.

paññāsaṅkhātaṃ.meaning_2: called 'wisdom'; designated as wisdom; reckoned as knowledge
paññāsaṅkhātaṃ.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a kammadhāraya compound where 'saṅkhāta' (called/designated) functions as an adjective modifying 'paññā' (wisdom). The compound means 'what is called wisdom' or 'designated as wisdom', suggesting a conceptual or conventional understanding of wisdom rather than wisdom itself.

vipātentaṃ.meaning_2: destroys; ruins; causes to fall down
vipātentaṃ.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] The form 'vipātentaṃ' appears to be a present participle in the accusative singular masculine form (vipātentaṃ), meaning 'one who destroys' or 'destroying'. This is a causative formation from the root √pat (to fall), with the prefix vi- giving an intensive or destructive sense.

cittagahapativatthu.meaning_2: case of householder Citta; story of householder Citta; grounds regarding householder Citta
cittagahapativatthu.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This appears to be a Vinaya term referring to a specific case or story involving Citta the householder, who was a prominent lay disciple known for his Dhamma talks. The compound combines his name (Citta), status (gahapati), and the legal/doctrinal context (vatthu).

bhāvanamiccheyyāti.meaning_2: would desire cultivation; would want to develop; would wish for meditation
bhāvanamiccheyyāti.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a sandhi compound consisting of three elements: bhāvanā (cultivation/meditation) + iccheyya (3rd sg optative of icchati, 'would wish') + iti (thus). The optative mood indicates a hypothetical or potential desire for spiritual cultivation.

sudhammattheraṃ.meaning_2: elder Sudhamma; venerable monk named Sudhamma
sudhammattheraṃ.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a proper name compound consisting of the personal name 'Sudhamma' (meaning 'good dhamma' or 'excellent qualities') combined with the title 'thera' (elder). The word appears to be in accusative singular case (-ṃ ending), indicating it's the object of a verb in the sentence.

sotukāmomhīti.meaning_2: wanting to hear; wishing to listen (to)
sotukāmomhīti.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] The word appears to be a compound adjective meaning 'one who desires to hear/listen'. The form 'sotukāmomhīti' shows sandhi combination with 'amhi' (I am) and 'iti' (thus), suggesting a phrase like 'I am one who wants to hear, thus...'

āgatāmhā.meaning_2: we have come; we have arrived
āgatāmhā.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] The form 'āgatāmhā' is a 1st person plural perfect tense form meaning 'we have come/arrived'. It combines the past participle 'āgata' (come) with the 1st person plural perfect ending 'mhā' (we have). This is an alternative perfect formation where the participle serves as the verb stem with personal endings added.

khuddakamahantesu.meaning_2: small and great; minor and major; insignificant and important
khuddakamahantesu.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] The word appears to be a dvanda (copulative) compound combining 'khuddaka' (small/minor) and 'mahanta' (large/major), describing things of varying sizes or importance. The -esu ending indicates locative plural case.

ekakiccepi.meaning_2: a single obligation; one duty; a solitary task
ekakiccepi.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a compound of 'eka' (one) + 'kicca' (duty/obligation), meaning 'a single obligation' or 'one specific duty'. The word appears to be in nominative/accusative case, functioning as a neuter noun describing a particular task or responsibility.

sāriputtattherasa.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a sandhi compound combining 'sāriputta' (the chief disciple) with 'thera' (elder). The final 'a' of sāriputta elides before the 't' of thera, forming 'sāriputtatthera'. This construction is common in Pāḷi for referring to venerable monks with their proper names.

vaṅgantabrāhmaṇassa.meaning_2: the Brahman Vaṅganta; Vaṅganta the Brahman
vaṅgantabrāhmaṇassa.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a compound of the proper name Vaṅganta (Sāriputta's father) with brāhmaṇa, indicating his social status as a Brahman. The genitive case ending '-assa' shows possession or relationship.

āhāraparibhogamaṅgalepi.meaning_2: auspiciousness of consuming food; blessing of food consumption; prosperity through eating
āhāraparibhogamaṅgalepi.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This appears to be a compound describing the auspicious or blessed nature of consuming food. The context suggests it refers to the spiritual significance or proper attitude toward eating, possibly in a monastic or religious context where food consumption is seen as more than mere physical nourishment.

kaṇṇavijjhanamaṅgalepi.meaning_2: even the auspicious ceremony of ear-piercing; even ear-piercing ceremonies
kaṇṇavijjhanamaṅgalepi.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] The word appears to be a compound consisting of 'kaṇṇavijjhana' (ear-piercing), 'maṅgala' (auspicious ceremony), and the enclitic particle 'api' (even). This likely refers to traditional ear-piercing ceremonies considered auspicious events, with 'api' emphasizing that even such ceremonies are included in the context.

appodakamadhupāyasaṃ.meaning_2: a small amount of water and milk rice pudding with honey; little water and sweet kheer
appodakamadhupāyasaṃ.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This appears to be a sandhi compound combining two separate items - 'appodaka' (little water) and 'madhupāyasaṃ' (sweet milk pudding). The context suggests these are two distinct offerings or substances being referenced together, likely in a ritual or offering context where both water and sweet food are presented.

sakkāramassa.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] The word 'sakkāramassa' appears to be a compound of 'sakkāra' + 'assa' (genitive/dative singular). In context, it likely means 'honor/respect for him' or 'his honor/respect', showing the genitive/dative function of the '-assa' ending.

sākhāviṭapapalāsāni.meaning_2: branches, forked branches, and leaves; branches with foliage and leaves
sākhāviṭapapalāsāni.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This appears to be a compound formed through sandhi where multiple nouns (sākhā 'branches', viṭapa 'forked branches/canopy', palāsa 'leaves/foliage') are joined together with the neuter plural ending -āni. The word describes various parts of trees or plants, likely referring to their branches and foliage collectively.

devamārabrahmanāgasupaṇṇādīnaṃ.grammar: sandhi, masc + masc + masc + masc + masc + masc
devamārabrahmanāgasupaṇṇādīnaṃ.meaning_2: of gods, Māras, Brahmas, nāgas, supaṇṇas, and so on
devamārabrahmanāgasupaṇṇādīnaṃ.family_compound: deva māra brahma nāga supaṇṇa ādi
devamārabrahmanāgasupaṇṇādīnaṃ.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a sandhi compound consisting of multiple nouns in genitive plural form (devānaṃ + mārānaṃ + brahmānaṃ + nāgānaṃ + supaṇṇānaṃ + ādīnaṃ) that have been combined through sandhi rules. The word functions as a genitive plural compound meaning 'of gods, Māras, Brahmas, nāgas, supaṇṇas, and others' - listing various classes of beings in Buddhist cosmology.

vīsaticīvarasahassānipi.meaning_2: twenty thousand robes; twenty thousand robe-cloths
vīsaticīvarasahassānipi.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a compound numeral-noun combination where 'vīsati' (twenty) modifies 'cīvarasahassa' (thousand robes), creating the meaning 'twenty thousand robes'. The word appears in the accusative plural form 'vīsaticīvarasahassānipi' with the enclitic particle 'api' (also/even) attached.

iddhimayapattacīvarāgamananti.meaning_2: bowl and robe made of psychic power; psychic bowl and robe
iddhimayapattacīvarāgamananti.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This appears to be a compound describing magical requisites created through psychic power. The compound combines 'iddhimaya' (made of psychic power) with 'pattacīvara' (bowl and robe), suggesting these are monastic requisites magically produced rather than ordinary material objects.

muṇḍakasīse.meaning_2: on a shaven head; on a bald head; on the head of a shaveling
muṇḍakasīse.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash] The word `muṇḍakasīse` is the locative singular form of the compound `muṇḍakasīsa`. The compound means 'shaven head' or 'bald head', or 'the head of a shaveling'. The locative form therefore means 'on a shaven head' or 'on the head of a shaveling'. `muṇḍaka` here functions as an adjective ('shaven', 'bald') or a noun ('shaveling') modifying `sīsa` (head).

bhikkhunīupassaye.meaning_2: at the nun's residence; in the nun's quarters
bhikkhunīupassaye.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash] The word `bhikkhunīupassaye` is the locative singular form of the compound noun `bhikkhunīupassaya`. It indicates a location, specifically 'at' or 'in' the residence or quarters designated for nuns, combining `bhikkhunī` (nun) and `upassaya` (residence, quarters).

dānaveyyāvaṭikopi.meaning_2: even one in charge of offerings; also a manager of charity; even an attendant for gifts
dānaveyyāvaṭikopi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash] The word `dānaveyyāvaṭikopi` is a sandhi compound of `dānaveyyāvaṭiko` (masculine nominative singular) and the indeclinable particle `api` (even, also). The compound `dānaveyyāvaṭika` is formed from `dāna` (meaning giving, charity, or assigning responsibility as per `dāna 1.4`) and `veyyāvaṭika` (one who performs a service or duty, an attendant, a manager). `veyyāvaṭika` is derived from `veyyāvaṭi` (service, management) with the suffix `-ka`. The overall meaning indicates someone who manages affairs related to charity or gifts, with `api` adding emphasis.

paṇṇatthāya.meaning_2: for the purpose of a leaf; for the sake of a letter
paṇṇatthāya.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash] The word `paṇṇatthāya` is the dative singular form of the masculine compound `paṇṇattha`. It is formed by combining `paṇṇa` (meaning 'leaf' or 'letter' according to the entries) and `attha` (meaning 'purpose', 'sake', or 'benefit'). The dative ending `-āy` signifies 'for the purpose of' or 'for the sake of', hence the overall meaning 'for the purpose of a leaf' or 'for the sake of a letter'.

rājayuvarājādayo.meaning_2: kings, prince regents, and so on; etc.; those beginning with kings and prince regents
rājayuvarājādayo.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash] The word is a sandhi compound formed by 'rāja' (king), 'yuvarāja' (prince regent or heir apparent), and 'ādayo' (the nominative plural form of 'ādi', meaning 'and so on' or 'etc.'). The compound refers to a group that includes kings and prince regents among others. The plural ending '-ādayo' indicates 'those beginning with' or 'etc.' following the mentioned items. 'Rājayuvarājādayo' is the masculine nominative plural form of the compound 'rājayuvarājādi'.

gandhakuṭidvāraṃ.meaning_2: door of the perfumed hut; entrance to the Buddha's dwelling
gandhakuṭidvāraṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash] The word is a compound of `gandhakuṭi` (perfumed hut, an epithet for the Buddha's dwelling) and `dvāra` (door, entrance). The ending `ṃ` indicates the nominative or accusative singular neuter form of the compound noun.

rohitamaccharasadānasseva.meaning_2: carp; Cyprinus rohitaka; lit. red fish
rohitamaccharasadānasseva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word meaning 'red fish', referring to a carp. It is likely used here as a literal description or possibly metaphorically.

paṇḍitotveva.meaning_2: in the state of a learned person indeed
paṇḍitotveva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound of 'paṇḍitatta' (state of being learned) and 'eva' (indeed). The 'a' from 'paṇḍitatta' and the 'u' from 'utu' have merged and then combined with 'eva'.

mañcapīṭhādīni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'mañcapīṭhādīni' is a compound word meaning 'beds, chairs, and the like' or 'furniture etc.'. It's formed by combining 'mañcapīṭha' (bed and chair) with the suffix 'ādi' which signifies 'and so on' or 'etc.'.

tucchavihāraṃ.meaning_2: empty residence; empty dwelling; empty way of life; empty meditation attainment
tucchavihāraṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'tucchavihāraṃ' is a compound word formed by 'tuccha' (empty) and 'vihāra' (dwelling, monastery, mode of living, meditation attainment). The context would determine which specific meaning of 'vihāra' is intended.

kaṭṭhakaliṅgarāni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'kaṭṭha' (stick, log) and 'kaliṅgara' (log, piece of wood). In this context, it likely refers to a log made of wood, perhaps a piece of timber.

labhissāmāvusoti.meaning_2: we would get; we would obtain
labhissāmāvusoti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the first person plural conditional form of the verb 'labhati', meaning 'to get' or 'to obtain'. The suffix '-issāma' indicates the first person plural and the conditional mood. In context, it implies a hypothetical situation where 'we would get' or 'we would obtain' something.

pemagāravayuttaṃ.meaning_2: endowed with love and respect; affectionate and respectful
pemagāravayuttaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'pema' (love), 'gārava' (respect), and 'yutta' (endowed with). The combination suggests a state of being characterized by both affection and reverence.

idhāgacchantehīti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'idhāgacchantehīti' is a sandhi compound. Breaking it down, we get 'idhā' (here) + 'āgacchante' (coming, present participle, plural) + 'iti' (thus). The 'ā' in 'āgacchante' is lengthened due to sandhi with 'idhā'. The 'e' at the end of 'āgacchante' is an instrumental plural ending for participles. Thus, the word can be understood as 'here they coming thus' or 'coming here thus'.

vaṇṇasampatti.meaning_2: excellence; magnificence; splendour; beauty; prosperity; welfare; good fortune; success
vaṇṇasampatti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word vaṇṇasampatti is a compound word formed from 'vaṇṇa' (meaning beauty, appearance, colour, sort, caste, reason, letter, size, shape, praise, approval, value, good point, positive quality, excellent characteristic) and 'sampatti' (meaning prosperity, welfare, good fortune, success, achievement, attainment, excellence, magnificence, splendour, beauty, completeness, good state). In this context, it is likely referring to a state of great beauty or excellence, possibly in appearance or quality.

āhārajarūpavasena.meaning_2: having material form produced by nutrition; material form born from nutriment
āhārajarūpavasena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word appears to be a compound of 'āhāraja' (produced by nutrition) and 'rūpa' (form, matter). The overall meaning indicates a material form that is a result of nourishment or sustenance.

paṭisāmitakāle.meaning_2: time of being set in order; time of being kept away
paṭisāmitakāle.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'paṭisāmita' is the past participle of 'paṭisāmeti' (to set in order, to keep away), and 'kāla' means time. Therefore, 'paṭisāmitakāla' refers to the time when something is set in order or kept away.

candadevaputto.meaning_2: son of the moon-deity; a celestial being associated with the moon
candadevaputto.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound of 'canda' (moon) and 'devaputto' (son of a deity). It likely refers to a specific celestial being or a metaphorical description.

sūriyadevaputto.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'sūriya' (sun) and 'devaputta' (son of a god, minor deity). The meaning 'son of the sun deity' is derived from these components. The grammatical form suggests a masculine singular noun.

nemiādīnaṃ.meaning_2: having rims and so on; consisting of wheels and so on
nemiādīnaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound adjective, formed by 'nemi' (rim of a wheel) and 'ādi' (and so on, etc.). The '-naṃ' ending indicates the genitive plural, meaning 'of those having rims and so on'. It's likely describing a collection of things that include wheels or have wheel-like structures as a part of them.

sotāpattimaggādīni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'sotāpatti' (stream entry, the first stage of sainthood) and 'magga' (path). The 'ādi' suffix here is in its pronominal sense of 'etc.; and so on; and so forth', indicating that the path of stream entry and similar concepts are included. This is a common usage in Buddhist texts to list a primary item and then indicate that other related items are also part of the discussion.

anunayavasena.meaning_2: due to affection; by means of affection
anunayavasena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound of 'anunay' (affection, inclination) and 'vasena' (due to, by means of). The meaning is 'due to affection' or 'by means of affection', indicating the cause or reason for something.

kāṇamātuvatthu.meaning_2: the case of the blind mother
kāṇamātuvatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of kāṇa (blind), mātu (mother, genitive of mātar), and vatthu (matter, case). It refers to a specific situation or case involving someone referred to as the 'blind mother'. The genitive form of mātar is used here in a compound construction.

mahallakabhikkhūhi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound of 'mahallaka' (elderly, old) and 'bhikkhūhi' (by monks, the instrumental plural of 'bhikkhu'). The word 'mahallakabhikkhūhi' therefore means 'by elderly monks'.

vacanakārikā.meaning_2: explanation of words; application of terms; interpretation of phrases; grammatical explanation
vacanakārikā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word appears to be a compound of 'vacana' (word, utterance) and 'kārikā' (doing, performance, commentary). In the context of linguistic or grammatical discussions, it likely refers to an explanation or interpretation of words or terms, perhaps a commentary or analysis of grammatical constructions.

cattālīsayojanasahassamatte.meaning_2: of forty thousand yojanas; approximately 800,000 kilometres
cattālīsayojanasahassamatte.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is an adverbial compound indicating a vast distance. The word 'matta' here functions similarly to an adverb, signifying 'to the extent of' or 'amounting to'. The combined meaning is 'amounting to forty thousand yojanas'.

catuyojanasahassamatte.meaning_2: measuring four thousand yojanas; approximately eighty thousand kilometers; a vast distance
catuyojanasahassamatte.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound describing a large distance. It combines 'catuyojana' (four yojanas) with 'sahassa' (thousand) and 'matta' (measure/amount). The combined meaning is a measure of four thousand yojanas. The suffix '-te' is a neuter plural locative or accusative ending, indicating 'in' or 'to' that measure. In the context of the sentence, it refers to a very great distance.

bhojetukāmo.meaning_2: wishing to feed; wanting to feed; would be delighted to feed
bhojetukāmo.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound, combining the causative infinitive stem of 'bhuñjati' (to eat) with the adjective 'kāmo' (wishing to). Therefore, it means 'wishing to feed someone'.

gadrabhayoniyaṃ.meaning_2: belonging to the womb of a donkey; of a donkey's birth
gadrabhayoniyaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'gadrabha' (donkey) and 'yoni' (womb/birth), with the adjectival suffix '-ya'. It describes something related to the birth or origin from a donkey.

ājānīyasindhavānaṃ.meaning_2: of thoroughbred Sindh horses; noble Sindhu steeds
ājānīyasindhavānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound adjective formed from 'ājānīya' (thoroughbred) and 'sindhavānaṃ' (of Sindh horses). The genitive plural ending '-ānaṃ' indicates possession or relation, meaning 'of thoroughbred Sindh horses' or 'belonging to thoroughbred Sindh horses'.

pitvāna.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The gerund 'pitvāna' is derived from the root √pā (to drink) and indicates an action completed before another action. It functions similarly to the English past participle 'having drunk'.

pivitvāna.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a gerund form indicating an action completed before the main verb. The root is related to drinking.

bhavanissitā.meaning_2: dependent on existence; resting on being; relying on becoming
bhavanissitā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'bhava' (existence, becoming) and 'nissita' (dependent, relying on). It describes something that is dependent on or relies upon the state of being or existence.

nibbānapāragāmino.meaning_2: going to the far shore of Nibbāna; leading to the far shore of Nibbāna
nibbānapāragāmino.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This compound word describes something or someone that is moving towards, or leads to, the ultimate goal of Nibbāna, which is understood as the 'far shore' of existence and suffering. It is a metaphorical expression emphasizing the profound spiritual destination.

cariyapaṭipakkhaṃ.meaning_2: contrary to conduct; contrary to behaviour; opposed to one's way of behaving; opposed to one's state of life

udakavāraṃ.comment: [openrouter: x-ai/grok-4-fast:free] The compound udakavāraṃ is in accusative singular, likely masculine following the gender of vāra. Without provided sentences, the meaning is inferred from components: udaka as 'water' (nt) and vāra as 'occasion' (masc) or 'sieve' (masc), possibly referring to a device or time related to water in Pāli texts.

udakamāharanti.comment: [openrouter: x-ai/grok-4-fast:free] Sandhi form combining accusative singular neuter 'udakam' (water) with 3rd plural present 'āharanti' (they bring/fetch), likely in a context of procuring water.

catumāsaccayenapi.meaning_2: even after the four months; even upon the lapse of the four-month period
catumāsaccayenapi.comment: [openrouter: x-ai/grok-4-fast:free] In Pāḷi texts, particularly in monastic contexts like the Vinaya, 'catumāsa' refers to the four-month rainy season retreat (vassa); the compound indicates 'even after that period has elapsed', emphasizing no exception even after the standard time.

kheḷasiṅghāṇikādīhi.meaning_2: spit and snot etc.; saliva and nasal mucus etc.
kheḷasiṅghāṇikādīhi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'kheḷasiṅghāṇikā' (spit and snot) and 'ādi' (etc.). The 'ādi' part functions here as an indeclinable suffix, indicating 'and so on'.

asuddhatarañceva.meaning_2: even dirtier; even more unclean; even more impure
asuddhatarañceva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound of 'asuddhatara' (dirtier, more unclean, more impure), 'ca' (and, also), and 'eva' (even, indeed). The meaning is 'and even dirtier' or 'and also even more impure'. The 'añ' in 'asuddhatarañceva' is a result of the sandhi rule where 'r' before 'c' causes 'ñ' to be inserted.

khantimettodakena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by three distinct nouns: 'khanti' (patience), 'mettā' (friendliness), and 'udaka' (water). The suffix '-a' with the masculine pattern indicates that this compound is being used as a masculine noun, likely referring to a concept or quality that embodies all three elements. The context of the sentence would further clarify its precise usage.

verūpasamanasaṅkhāto.meaning_2: so called as having calming hatred; settling ill-will; appeasing animosity
verūpasamanasaṅkhāto.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'verūpasamana' (calming hatred) and 'saṅkhāta' (reckoned, so called). The combination indicates something that is 'called' or 'defined' as having achieved the state of calming hatred.

vīhipaharaṇakāle.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word refers to the specific time when paddy is threshed.

musalasālāya.meaning_2: hall for maces; hall for pestles; hall for shovels; hall for stables
musalasālāya.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word appears to be a compound of 'musala' (mace, pestle, or shovel) and 'sālā' (hall). The exact meaning depends on which sense of 'musala' is intended, and likely refers to a place where these items are kept or used.

aggayāgubhattādīni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'aggayāgubhatta' is a compound word formed from 'agga' (best) and 'yāgubhatta' (rice gruel). Therefore, 'aggayāgubhatta' means 'best rice-gruel'.

yāvajjakālā.meaning_2: as long as; for the time being
yāvajjakālā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'yāva' (as long as) and 'kāla' (time). It functions as an adverb meaning 'as long as' or 'for the time being'.

ākāsaṭṭhadevatāpīti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of ākāsa (sky), ṭha (standing, residing), and devatā (deity). It refers to deities who reside or stand in the sky. The word is in the feminine gender, as indicated by the pattern 'ā fem' and the feminine grammatical marker in the related entry for lemma_1.

dhammakathikaantevāsikānaṃ.meaning_2: disciples of Dhamma preachers; students of Dhamma teachers
dhammakathikaantevāsikānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'dhammakathika' (Dhamma preacher) and 'antevāsika' (apprentice, student). The genitive plural ending '-ānaṃ' indicates possession or relation, so it means 'of the disciples of Dhamma preachers'.

māritabhāvañceva.meaning_2: the fact of having been killed; state of being dead
māritabhāvañceva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word describes the state of being killed. The 'ca' likely connects this to a preceding or following condition or event, and 'eva' emphasizes this state, possibly to the exclusion of other states.

yathāha.meaning_2: as he said; thus he said; as it is said; like this
yathāha.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound of 'yathā' (as, like) and 'āha' (he said). It functions as a perfect tense verb, indicating that something was said in a manner described by 'yathā'.

hatthīnīhi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the instrumental plural form of the word 'hatthī' (elephant). The instrumental case often indicates the agent or instrument by which an action is performed. In this context, 'hatthīnīhi' would mean 'by the elephants'.

dārudaṇḍakena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'dāru' (wood) and 'daṇḍaka' (rod, stick). The suffix '-ena' indicates the instrumental case, meaning 'with a wooden rod' or 'by means of a wooden rod'.

tattabhāvaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'tatta' (real, true) and 'bhāva' (state, nature). It signifies the true or real state or nature of something.

bījati.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The sentence context would determine if 'bījati' refers to literally sowing seed or metaphorically sowing something.

vāḷamigaparipanthanivāraṇatthaṃ.meaning_2: wild beast; fierce animal; beast of prey; obstacle; obstruction; blocking; warding off; for the purpose of
vāḷamigaparipanthanivāraṇatthaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. The word 'atthaṃ' functions adverbially here, indicating 'for the purpose of' or 'for the sake of'. Therefore, the entire phrase means 'for the purpose of warding off obstacles of wild beasts'.

antarantarena.meaning_2: in between; within each other; mutually
antarantarena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'antarāntarena' is a compound adjective formed by repeating the word 'antara'. It signifies a state of being 'in between' or 'within' each other, implying mutual relationship or interdependency within a context.

pālileyyakarakkhitavanasaṇḍo.meaning_2: name of a town near Kosambī; name of a forest; lit. protected forest grove
pālileyyakarakkhitavanasaṇḍo.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The compound word pālileyyakarakkhitavanasaṇḍo is a sandhi form of pālileyyaka + rakkhitavanasaṇḍa. The text refers to the Pālileyya forest.

mukhodakadānaṃ.meaning_2: giving water for washing the face or rinsing the mouth; gift of mouth-water
mukhodakadānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'mukhodaka' (water for washing the face/rinsing the mouth) and 'dāna' (giving/gift). Therefore, it means the act of giving or a gift of such water.

tenevūpāyena.meaning_2: by that means; by that method; by such a stratagem
tenevūpāyena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound formed from 'tena' (by that), 'eva' (indeed, only) and 'upāya' (means, method, stratagem). It functions as an adverb meaning 'by that means' or 'by such a stratagem', indicating the manner or method by which something is done.

sabbavattāni.meaning_2: all customs; all practices; all duties; all services
sabbavattāni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'sabba' (all) and 'vatta' (custom, practice, duty, service). In the context of the sentence, it refers to 'all the duties' or 'all the services' of the monks.

paribhogamakāsi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'paribhoga' (enjoyment, use) and 'akāsi' (did, performed), which is the aorist of the verb 'karoti' (to do). Thus, 'paribhogamakāsi' means 'did enjoyment' or 'performed use', translating to 'enjoyed' or 'used'.

akkantasākhāpi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word appears to be a compound of 'akkanta' (stepped on/trod on), 'sākhā' (branch), and 'api' (an indeclinable particle, likely 'even' or 'also' in this context). The full meaning would depend on the sentence it is used in, but it could suggest something like 'even on the branches that were trodden upon'.

khāṇumatthake.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word appears to be a sandhi compound formed from 'khāṇu' (tree stump) and 'matthake' (locative singular of 'matthaka', meaning 'top' or 'distance'). Given the context of the word in a sentence would be essential for a more precise interpretation, but it likely refers to the 'top of a tree stump' or possibly 'a distance from a tree stump', depending on the specific idiomatic usage.

niviṭṭhagatto.meaning_2: having limbs firmly established; with body parts settled
niviṭṭhagatto.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This compound adjective describes a state where the limbs or body parts are firmly set or established, implying a stable or even rigid posture.

makkaṭadevaputto.meaning_2: a monkey-god; a god who is a monkey
makkaṭadevaputto.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'makkaṭa' (monkey) and 'devaputta' (minor god/young deity). In the context of the sentence, it refers to a specific type of divine being that is both a monkey and a god.

sāvatthinagarato.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by combining the proper noun 'Sāvatthī' (a city) and 'nagara' (city). The suffix '-to' indicates the ablative case, meaning 'from Sāvatthī city'.

mahāupāsikātievamādīni.meaning_2: great female disciple; eminent female devotee
mahāupāsikātievamādīni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by mahā (great) and upāsikā (female devotee/disciple). The 'iti' and 'evamādi' are implied by the context, suggesting 'and other great female disciples'.

pālileyyako.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'pālileyyako' appears to be a vocative form of the masculine noun 'pālileyya', which is the name of a town near Kosambī. The addition of 'ko' (a vocative marker derived from the pronoun 'ka') suggests it is being used in direct address.

daṇḍamādāya.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'daṇḍamādāya' is a compound formed from 'daṇḍa' (stick, club, punishment) and 'ādāya' (gerund of the verb 'ādiyati', meaning 'taking', 'holding', 'carrying', 'with'). In this context, it most likely means 'taking a stick' or 'with a stick', implying the use of a weapon or instrument for punishment or enforcement.

nisīdanapāsāṇaphalake.meaning_2: a stone slab for sitting on
nisīdanapāsāṇaphalake.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound of 'nisīdana' (sitting cloth/mat) and 'pāsāṇaphalaka' (stone slab). The context suggests a stone slab used as a sitting mat or place.

vattapaṭivattakārakopi.meaning_2: doer of duties and minor responsibilities; performer of mundane tasks; agent of recurrent duties
vattapaṭivattakārakopi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word vattapaṭivattakārakopi is a sandhi compound. The 'api' at the end is an indeclinable particle. In this context, it functions to add emphasis or inclusivity, meaning 'even the doer of duties and minor responsibilities' or 'also the performer of mundane tasks'.

pacchāmukhakaraṇaṃ.meaning_2: turning west; causing to face west
pacchāmukhakaraṇaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'pacchāmukha' means 'heading west' and 'karaṇa' means 'doing' or 'causing'. Therefore, 'pacchāmukhakaraṇa' means 'the act of causing something to face west'.

kālattheravatthu.meaning_2: case of time for an elder monk
kālattheravatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'Kāla' refers to 'time' or 'occasion'. 'Thera' means 'elder monk'. 'Vatthu' in this context signifies a 'case' or 'matter'. Therefore, kālattheravatthu translates to 'case of time for an elder monk', likely referring to specific rules or considerations regarding time for senior monks within the monastic community.

kālattheraṃ.meaning_2: time; occasion; suitable time; appropriate occasion; right time; lit. time
kālattheraṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the stem 'kāla' (time) with an adverbial suffix '-m' (interpreted as '-ṃ' in the text 'kālattheraṃ') which forms an adverbial phrase 'kālaṃ theraṃ'. This means 'for a long time'.

paṭivissakagehe.meaning_2: house of a neighbour; neighbour's dwelling
paṭivissakagehe.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'paṭivissaka' (neighbour) and 'geha' (house). The ending '-gehe' indicates a locative case, meaning 'in the house of a neighbour'.

punadivasepīti.meaning_2: on the following day; even on the next day
punadivasepīti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'punadivasepīti' is a sandhi compound. 'punadivase' is the locative singular of 'punadivasa' meaning 'following day'. 'pi' is an enclitic particle meaning 'even' or 'also'. 'iti' is a particle indicating the end of a quote or a word, often functioning like 'thus' or 'so'. In this context, 'punadivasepīti' combines these elements to mean 'and even on the following day', suggesting an emphasis on the events of the next day.

dhītāpissā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word dhītāpissā is a sandhi compound. The first part, dhītā, means 'daughter'. The second part, pissā, is derived from the verb āpeti, meaning 'to reach' or 'to attain', and here it is in the conditional mood, implying 'would have caused to reach' or 'would have caused to attain'. Therefore, dhītāpissā likely means 'would have caused the daughter to reach/attain'.

tassajjhāsayaṃ.construction: adhi > adhy > ajjh + ā + √si > say + *a + aṃ
tassajjhāsayaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is an adverbial accusative form of 'ajjhāsaya' (purpose, determination). It functions to describe the manner or circumstance, indicating that something is done 'regarding the purpose' or 'with determination'.

sakkārahānibhayena.meaning_2: fear of honour; fear of respect
sakkārahānibhayena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'sakkāra' (honour), 'hāni' (loss, decline), and 'bhaya' (fear). The construction indicates a fear that arises from the loss or decline of honour or respect.

veḷusaṅkhātassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a tatpurusha compound where the first element 'veḷu' (bamboo) modifies the second element 'saṅkhāta' (called, named). Therefore, it means 'that which is called or named bamboo'.

ghātatthameva.meaning_2: for the purpose of destruction; for destruction
ghātatthameva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'ghāta' (destruction) and 'attha' (purpose, benefit). In this context, it means 'for the purpose of destruction' or 'for destruction'.

cūḷakālaupāsakavatthu.meaning_2: the minor occasion of the lay devotee; a minor event concerning a lay devotee
cūḷakālaupāsakavatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. The meaning is derived from the combination of its parts: 'cūḷa' (minor), 'kāla' (occasion), 'upāsaka' (lay devotee), and 'vatthu' (matter/case). In the context of Vinaya, 'vatthu' often refers to a case or incident.

cūḷakālaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound of 'cūḷa' (lesser, smaller) and 'kāla' (time). In this context, it functions as an adverb meaning 'for a short time' or 'briefly'.

mahākālavatthusmiṃ.meaning_2: Great time; opportune moment; auspicious time; the great period of time.
mahākālavatthusmiṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'mahā' (great) and 'kāla' (time). In the context of a sentence, it would refer to a significant or auspicious period of time.

pothayiṃsu.meaning_2: they beat; they hit; they hurt; they killed
pothayiṃsu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word pothayiṃsu is the 3rd person plural aorist form of the verb pothayati, meaning to beat, hit, hurt, or kill. The 'iṃsu' ending clearly indicates the 3rd person plural aorist. Therefore, the sentence describes multiple subjects performing the action of beating, hitting, hurting, or killing.

cūḷakālaupāsako.meaning_2: a junior devotee; a junior lay follower
cūḷakālaupāsako.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'cūḷa' (lesser/junior), 'kāla' (time/period), and 'upāsaka' (lay disciple/devotee). The compound likely refers to a devotee who is junior in status or has been recently initiated.

akaraṇabhāvena.meaning_2: non-doing; abstention; non-performance; lack of action
akaraṇabhāvena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'akaraṇabhāvena' is a compound formed from 'akaraṇa' (non-doing, abstention) and 'bhāva' (state, nature). It is used in the instrumental case, indicating 'by means of non-doing' or 'through abstention'.

sugatiñceva.meaning_2: and good destination; and happy fate
sugatiñceva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'sugatiñca' is a sandhi compound of 'sugati' (good destination, happy fate) and 'ca' (and). The contextual meaning is 'and a good destination' or 'and a happy fate'.

kusalakammasaṅkhātā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'kusala' (wholesome, skilful) and 'kamma' (action, deed). It refers to actions that are morally good or beneficial.

akusalakammasaṅkhātā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word meaning 'unwholesome action' or 'unskilful deed'.

kārakasattānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The form kārakasattānaṃ is genitive plural. The lemma is kāraka, meaning 'doer' or 'agent'. The word 'sattānaṃ' is genitive plural of 'satta' meaning 'being' or 'creature'. Therefore, kārakasattānaṃ means 'of the doers of beings' or 'of the creators of creatures'.

cūḷakālo.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'cūḷā' (crest, plume, lock of hair, but here used in a figurative sense of 'lesser' or 'minor') and 'kāla' (time). Thus, 'cūḷakāla' means 'lesser time' or 'shorter duration'.

attadatthattheravatthu.meaning_2: the topic/case concerning one's own welfare and the elder
attadatthattheravatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound formed by joining 'attadattha' (one's own welfare) with 'thera' (elder) and 'vatthu' (topic/case). The meaning in context is the topic or case related to the elder's own welfare.

attadatthattheraṃ.meaning_2: one who looks after his own welfare and is also an elder monk; a senior monk who looks after his own welfare
attadatthattheraṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. The first part, 'attadattha', means 'one's own welfare' or 'personal benefit'. The second part, 'thera', refers to an elder or a senior monk. Therefore, 'attadatthatthera' describes a senior monk who is also concerned with or focused on his own welfare.

uppannasaṃvegā.meaning_2: a sense of urgency that has arisen; a religious emotion that has arisen
uppannasaṃvegā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'uppanna' (arisen, appeared) and 'saṃvega' (dismay, anxiety, sense of urgency, religious emotion). The context would determine whether it refers to a general sense of urgency or a specific religious emotion that has arisen.

attadatthatthero.meaning_2: an elder who looks after his own welfare
attadatthatthero.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'Attadatthathera' is composed of 'attadatthā' (one's own welfare/benefit) and 'thera' (elder/senior monk). The context suggests an elder monk who is focused on his personal benefit or welfare. The 'o' ending in 'attadatthathero' is the vocative singular case ending for masculine nouns.

gandhādīhi.meaning_2: smells etc.; perfumes etc.; fragrances etc.
gandhādīhi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word gandhādīhi is a sandhi compound. The ending -hi indicates the instrumental plural. Therefore, gandhādīhi means 'by/with smells etc.' or 'perfumes etc.' This word is a compound of 'gandha' (smell, perfume, fragrance) and 'ādi' (etc., and so on). The meaning of 'gandha' here is likely related to scents or perfumes as it is often associated with pleasant smells. The 'ādi' serves to include other related items in the same category.

attadatthasadiseneva.meaning_2: similar to one's own welfare; similar to personal benefit
attadatthasadiseneva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'attadatthasadisa' is a compound word. It is formed by 'attadatthā' (one's own welfare; personal benefit) and 'sadisa' (similar to). The meaning 'similar to one's own welfare' indicates a comparison to what benefits oneself.

kākaṇikamattampi.meaning_2: amounting to a kākaṇikā; a very small amount
kākaṇikamattampi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of kākaṇikā (a coin of very low value) and matta (amount of, measure of). Therefore, kākaṇikamattampi means 'even the amount of a kākaṇikā', signifying a very small quantity.

sahassamattenāpi.meaning_2: by a thousand; amounting to a thousand
sahassamattenāpi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound adjective formed from 'sahassa' (thousand) and 'matta' (amount of, measured). In this context, it signifies 'by a thousand' or 'amounting to a thousand'.

kākaṇikamattenāpi.meaning_2: by the amount of a kākaṇikā (a coin of very low value); for a mere trifle
kākaṇikamattenāpi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word combines 'kākaṇikā', meaning a very small coin, with 'mattena', the instrumental singular of 'matta' (amount, measure). The phrase conveys the idea of something being of negligible value, as if bought for a tiny amount.

kammaṭṭhānasīsena.meaning_2: meditation subject; meditation object; theme for reflection
kammaṭṭhānasīsena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'kamma' (work, deed) and 'ṭhāna' (place, station). In the context of meditation, it refers to the object or subject of contemplation. The given suffix '-ena' indicates the instrumental case, suggesting 'by means of a meditation subject'.

cetiyapaṭisaṅkharaṇādikiccaṃ.meaning_2: the work etc. of restoring or repairing shrines
cetiyapaṭisaṅkharaṇādikiccaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'Cetiya' refers to a shrine or stupa. 'Paṭisaṅkharaṇa' means restoration or repair. 'Ādi' means etc. or and so on, indicating that there are other related tasks. 'Kicca' means work or duty. Therefore, the compound refers to the tasks associated with shrine restoration and repair, among other things.

upajjhāyādivattaṃ.meaning_2: the custom or duty of a preceptor, including etc.
upajjhāyādivattaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'upajjhāyā' (preceptress), 'ādi' (etc., and so on), and 'vatta' (custom, practice, duty). In this context, it refers to the duties and practices associated with a preceptor, including a list of other related matters.

ābhisamācārikavattañhi.meaning_2: related to excellent conduct; regarding points of etiquette
ābhisamācārikavattañhi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound adjective meaning 'related to excellent conduct' or 'regarding points of etiquette'. It is derived from the noun abhisamācāra.

ariyaphalādīni.meaning_2: beginning with noble fruits; consisting of noble fruits and similar things
ariyaphalādīni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word is a compound of 'ariya phala' (noble fruit) and 'ādi' (etc.; and so on). In this context, it refers to things that are like or follow after noble fruits.

accāraddhavipassako.meaning_2: one who sees with excessive or over-stimulated clear insight; one who has clear insight which is too forcefully applied
accāraddhavipassako.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'accāraddha' (overly aroused, over-stimulated, too forcefully applied) and 'vipassako' (one who has clear insight). In the context of meditation, 'accāraddhavipassako' would refer to someone whose insight is too intense, perhaps leading to agitation or a lack of equanimity, rather than the balanced and steady insight sought in Vipassanā practice.

upajjhāyavattādīnipi.meaning_2: proper conduct toward the preceptor; duty toward a teacher
upajjhāyavattādīnipi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of `upajjhāya` (preceptor) and `vatta` (conduct, duty). It refers to the proper way of behaving towards one's teacher or preceptor.

uyyuttapayutto.meaning_2: deployed and applied; on active duty and intent
uyyuttapayutto.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word appears to be a sandhi compound of two past participles: 'uyyutta' (deployed, on active duty) and 'payutta' (applied, intent, devoted). The combined meaning suggests a state of being both militarily active and mentally engaged or devoted to a task.

sampattabhikkhūnampi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the past participle of the verb sampāpuṇāti, meaning 'to reach' or 'to arrive'. In this context, it describes the state of having arrived or being present.

attavaggavaṇṇanā.meaning_2: commentary on the Chapter on Self
attavaggavaṇṇanā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'attavagga' (Chapter 12 of the Dhammapada) and 'vaṇṇanā' (commentary). The meaning reflects a detailed explanation or exegesis of that specific chapter.

daharabhikkhuvatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'dahara' (young) and 'bhikkhu' (monk), referring to a junior monk.

niccapaññattā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This compound is formed by 'nicca' (permanent, lasting, ordered) and 'paññatta' (prepared, arranged, formulated, decreed, stated, declared, designated, assigned). In this context, it means something that is permanently established, appointed, or prescribed, likely referring to a rule or decree that is fixed and unchangeable.

parissāventī.meaning_2: cause to flow down; cause to drip; cause to flow
parissāventī.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a causative form of the root √su (to flow), with the prefix pari- (around, down). The -e- is a conjugational sign, and -ti is the 3rd person singular present tense verbal ending. In the context of the sentence, it means to cause something to flow down.

chinnakesanakhassa.meaning_2: having cut hair and nails; having cut hair and claws
chinnakesanakhassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound formed from 'chinna' (cut), 'kesa' (hair), 'nakha' (nail/claw), and 'kha' (space/sky, but here likely part of 'nakha' or a variant form). The meaning in context seems to be related to being 'cut' in terms of hair and nails, or possibly claws if 'kha' is considered in that way. Given the other lemmas, it is most likely referring to cut hair and nails.

chinnanivāsanapārupanassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] In this context, 'chinna' likely refers to something that is broken or damaged.

chinnakapālaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'chinnakapālaṃ' is a compound. 'chinna' (derived from √chid) typically means 'cut', but 'chinnaka' as an adjective can mean 'wanton' or 'shameless'. 'Pāla' means 'protector' or 'keeper'. Therefore, 'chinnakapālaṃ' likely refers to a 'protector of the shameless' or someone who enables or shelters loose morals. The '-ṃ' ending indicates the accusative case.

agarukanti.meaning_2: not heavy; not serious; not respected; not esteemed; not given importance
agarukanti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a present participle form, negated by 'na', meaning 'not being heavy, serious, or respected'. The suffix 'anti' indicates the third person plural ending.

chinnakesādibhāvaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This compound refers to the state of being without or devoid of hair etc. The 'chinna' here, used in a compound, takes on the meaning of 'without'.

chinnakesanakhavatthassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of four parts: chinna (cut off), kesa (hair), nakha (nail), and vatthu (cloth/garment). In this context, it refers to the state of being cut off or severed from hair, nails, and garments.

sotāpattiphalūpanissayaṃ.meaning_2: support for the fruit of entering the stream; reliance on the fruit of entering the stream
sotāpattiphalūpanissayaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'sotāpattiphala' (fruit of entering the stream) and 'upanissaya' (support, reliance). It refers to the support or reliance on the attainment of the first stage of enlightenment. The final 'ṃ' is a nasalization marker common in Pāḷi.

chinnakesādimattakeneva.meaning_2: without hair and the like, merely
chinnakesādimattakeneva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'chinna' means 'cut off' or 'without'. 'kesādi' refers to hair and the like. 'mattaka' means 'mere' or 'simple'. 'iva' means 'like' or 'as'. Therefore, 'chinnakesādimattakeneva' can be understood as 'merely without hair and the like'.

anukulabhāvaṃ.meaning_2: accordance; agreement; harmony; lit. state of being according to
anukulabhāvaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word denotes a state of being in accordance or agreement. It is formed by combining the adjective 'anukula' (meaning according to tradition, following family custom) with the abstract noun 'bhāva' (meaning state or condition).

hasanabhāvo.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'hasana' (laughter) and 'bhāva' (state, condition). Therefore, 'hasanabhāvo' means the 'state of laughter' or 'one who is in a state of laughter'.

oṭṭhagoṇādīhipi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'oṭṭha' refers to the lip or lips. It is masculine in gender.

nibbattāpetīti.meaning_2: causes to arise; causes to be born; causes to be produced
nibbattāpetīti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a causative form. The root is √vatt (to go, proceed, turn), with the prefix nī- (out, down). The causative suffix -āpeti is added to create the meaning of causing something to arise or be born. The 'ti' ending indicates the 3rd person singular present tense.

sativossaggalakkhaṇena.meaning_2: by the characteristic of the relinquishment of mindfulness
sativossaggalakkhaṇena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound. 'sati' here likely refers to a deluded or mistaken mindfulness, contrasting with the positive 'sati' (mindfulness) found elsewhere. 'vossaggam' means relinquishment or release. 'lakkhaṇam' means characteristic or sign. Therefore, the compound describes a characteristic of the relinquishment of this mistaken mindfulness.

suddhodanavatthu.meaning_2: related to Suddhodana; the place or estate belonging to Suddhodana
suddhodanavatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'Suddhodana' is the name of the Buddha's father, a king of the Sakyans. 'Vatthu' in this context, as per the dictionary entries, refers to 'land', 'property', 'ground', or 'site'. Therefore, 'Suddhodanavatthu' likely refers to the land, property, or estate belonging to King Suddhodana.

paṭhamagamanena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'paṭhamagamanena' is a compound word. The first part 'paṭhama' means 'first' and 'gamana' means 'going' or 'arrival'. Therefore, 'paṭhamagamanena' means 'by the first arrival'.

katapaccuggamano.meaning_2: going back after having done; returning after completion
katapaccuggamano.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word `katapaccuggama` appears to be a compound word. Let's break it down: `kata` (done) + `pacca` (back, behind, again - likely a prefix in this context) + `ugga` (rising, going up) + `gama` (going). Considering the provided dictionary entries, `ugga` can be related to `ud √gam` (to go up). The `pacca` here seems to function as a prefix indicating 'back' or 'again'. Therefore, `katapaccuggama` could mean 'going back after having done something' or 'returning after completion'.

mānabhindanatthāya.meaning_2: for the purpose of breaking down pride; for the destruction of conceit
mānabhindanatthāya.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word in the dative case, functioning adverbially, indicating purpose. It combines 'māna' (pride), 'bhindana' (breaking), and 'attha' (purpose/benefit).

ratanacaṅkamaṃ.meaning_2: precious walking meditation path; treasure walking meditation path
ratanacaṅkamaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'ratana' (jewel, treasure) and 'caṅkama' (walking meditation path). The meaning in context suggests a path that is either very beautiful and precious like a jewel, or a path used for walking meditation in a treasured or important location.

suddhodanamahārājānaṃ.meaning_2: name of the Buddha's father; king of the Sakyans
suddhodanamahārājānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of suddha (pure) and odana (cooked rice), referring to the king who provided pure sustenance. The ending '-mahārājānaṃ' is the genitive plural of mahārāja, indicating possession or relation. Thus, 'suddhodanamahārājānaṃ' translates to 'of King Suddhodana'.

vassiyevāti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the present tense of the verb "vassiyati", which means 'to rain'. The ending '-yati' indicates the third person singular present tense.

atītabuddhā.14: This is a compound word formed from 'atīta' (past) and 'vihāra' (dwelling, abode). The sentence likely refers to dwelling places or states that have passed or are no longer present.

paṭhamagehato.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word, 'paṭhamagehato', is a compound word. 'paṭhama' means 'first', and 'geha' means 'house'. Therefore, 'paṭhamagehato' likely refers to 'the first house' or 'the foremost dwelling'. The presence of the '-to' ending suggests it might be in the genitive or dative case, indicating possession or a recipient of the 'first house'.

saṇṭhāpento.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the present tense, third person singular of the causative verb saṇṭhāpeti, derived from the root √ṭhā (to stand). The prefix saṃ- intensifies the meaning, leading to senses like 'to cause to stand together', 'to establish', or 'to settle'. In the context of a sentence, it would likely mean that someone or something is causing a situation, a place, or a condition to be established or settled.

suvaṇṇasivikādīhi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound. The first part 'suvaṇṇa' means 'golden', and 'sivikā' means 'litter' or 'palanquin'. The suffix 'ādi' signifies 'etc.' or 'and so on'. The ending '-hi' indicates the instrumental plural case. Therefore, the entire word translates to 'by golden litters and the like'.

jīvanavaṃso.meaning_2: livelihood of the lineage; heritage of subsistence
jīvanavaṃso.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'jīvana' (life, livelihood) and 'vaṃsa' (lineage, heritage). The meaning in context suggests the inheritance or continuation of one's means of subsistence through family or lineage.

gahetabbapiṇḍe.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a potential participle, indicating something that 'should be taken' or 'is to be grasped'. In the context of the provided (but unseen) sentence, it likely refers to a specific item or concept that is meant to be understood or adopted.

piṇḍacārikavattañhi.meaning_2: the custom/practice of going for alms
piṇḍacārikavattañhi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'piṇḍacārikavattañhi' is a sandhi compound of 'piṇḍacārikā' (adj: who goes to collect alms) and 'vatta' (nt: custom; practice; way of life; behaviour). The 'hi' at the end is an indeclinable particle adding emphasis.

bhikkhācariyadhammaṃ.meaning_2: wandering for alms; roaming for food; the practice of going for alms
bhikkhācariyadhammaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'bhikkhācariyadhammaṃ' is a compound word. The first part, 'bhikkhācariyā', refers to the act of going for alms. The second part, 'dhammaṃ', in this context, refers to the practice or way of life. Therefore, 'bhikkhācariyadhammaṃ' translates to 'the practice of going for alms'.

vesiyādibhede.meaning_2: prostitute, whore; and so on, etc. (referring to types of prostitutes or related aspects)
vesiyādibhede.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound, formed by 'vesiyā' (prostitute) and 'ādi' (etc.; and so on). The meaning in context would likely be 'prostitutes and the like' or 'various kinds of prostitutes'.

vuttatthameva.meaning_2: with the meaning spoken of; of that meaning indeed
vuttatthameva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound formed from 'vutta' (said, spoken), 'attha' (meaning), and 'eva' (indeed, only). It functions as an adverb, emphasizing that something is precisely of the meaning that has been stated or discussed.

pañcasatavipassakabhikkhuvatthu.meaning_2: the case of five hundred monks with clear insight
pañcasatavipassakabhikkhuvatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'pañcasata' means 'five hundred'. 'vipassaka' means 'who has clear insight'. 'bhikkhu' means 'monk'. 'vatthu' in the context of the Vinaya refers to a 'case' or 'instance'. Therefore, the entire word means 'the case of five hundred monks who have clear insight'.

appavisesā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'appavisesā' is a compound adjective formed from 'appa' (not, without) and 'avisesa' (difference). Therefore, 'appavisesa' means 'without difference' or 'similar'.

pālileyyakahatthinā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a toponym, referring to the town of Pāileyyaka. The 'hatthinā' likely indicates an elephant associated with this place, perhaps a royal elephant or a herd.

ekacārikabhāvova.meaning_2: the state of wandering alone; a solitary life
ekacārikabhāvova.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'ekacārika' (wandering alone) and 'bhāva' (state, condition). Therefore, it refers to the condition or state of being a solitary wanderer or living alone.

nivattetukāmoti.meaning_2: wishing to stop; wanting to stop; wishing to turn away; wanting to turn away
nivattetukāmoti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. The components are 'nivattetuṃ' (infinitive of nivatteti, meaning 'to stop' or 'to turn away'), 'kāma' (adjective meaning 'wishing to' or 'wanting to'), and 'iti' (an indeclinable particle meaning 'thus' or 'so'). The entire word functions as an indeclinable adverbial phrase indicating a desire to stop or turn away.

pālileyyakadevaputtoyevassa.meaning_2: name of a town near Kosambī
pālileyyakadevaputtoyevassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a toponym, referring to a town. The construction indicates it is derived from 'palila' (related to 'palila' meaning 'a marsh' or 'a swampy place') with the addition of suffixes '-eyya' and '-ka', suggesting a place associated with such conditions or a place name formed in a particular way.

porāṇakapaṇḍitāpi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'porāṇa' (ancient) and 'paṇḍita' (wise man). In the given context, it describes someone who is both ancient and wise.

voropiyamānesupi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a past participle derived from the root √var, meaning 'to pluck' or 'to remove'. In the context of the sentence, it likely describes something that has been plucked or removed.

paviṭṭhakkhaṇeyeva.meaning_2: even those who have entered; even those who have entered
paviṭṭhakkhaṇeyeva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound of paviṭṭha (entered), akkhaṇa (time/moment), and eva (even/indeed). The contextually most likely meaning for 'akkhaṇa' here is 'time' or 'moment', making the phrase 'even those who have entered at the right moment' or 'even those who have entered at an opportune time'.

pubbaḷake.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word "pubbaḷake" appears to be a locative plural form of "pubbaḷaka". The meaning "a kind of bird" is inferred from the likely context of Pāli texts which often mention various animals and birds. The etymological breakdown suggests a connection to "pubba" (previous, eastern) and "aḷaka" (possibly related to a claw or a kingdom), which might hint at some characteristic of the bird, though its exact etymological significance in this context is not immediately clear without more information.

bhijjanatthena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word, meaning 'destruction' or 'breaking down', likely refers to the destruction of the 'anattha' (harm or misfortune) as implied by the context.

pubbuḷakasadisoyevāti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'pubbuḷaka' is likely being used metaphorically in relation to 'sadisa' (similar/like) and 'eva' (only/just) in a sentence that is not provided. Without the full sentence, a precise contextual meaning is impossible. However, given the 'dimin of pubbuḷa' and 'little bubble' meaning, it might refer to something ephemeral or insignificant that is still considered 'like' something else.

gehasaṇṭhānādivasena.meaning_2: according to house, shape, etc.; by means of house, shape, etc.
gehasaṇṭhānādivasena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound indicating 'according to house, shape, etc.'. The final component 'vasena' is an instrumental of 'divasa' (day), often used to mean 'by means of' or 'according to'.

rittatucchādibhāveneva.meaning_2: empty of empty things; utterly empty
rittatucchādibhāveneva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This compound intensifies the meaning of emptiness. 'ritta' itself means empty, and 'tuccha' also means empty.  The combination emphasizes a profound or complete emptiness.

khandhādilokaṃ.meaning_1: the world of aggregates and so on
khandhādilokaṃ.meaning_2: the world starting with the aggregates
khandhādilokaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'khandhā' is the plural of 'khandha' meaning aggregates or things clung to. 'ādi' means beginning with or etc. 'loka' means world. Therefore, the compound 'khandhādiloka' refers to the world of aggregates and subsequent phenomena, or simply 'the world and so forth'.

abhayarājakumāravatthu.meaning_2: the story of Prince Abhaya; case of Prince Abhaya
abhayarājakumāravatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'abhaya' is likely referring to a prince (lemma_1: abhaya 4), and 'rājakumāra' means prince. 'vatthu' in this context refers to a story or case, typical in the Vinaya.

abhayarājakumāraṃ.meaning_2: fearless prince; name of a prince; king Bimbisāra's son
abhayarājakumāraṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'abhaya' (fearless) and 'rājakumāra' (prince). The meaning is 'fearless prince'. Based on the dictionary entries, 'abhaya' can refer to a prince, and this specific compound likely refers to a prince named Abhayarājakumāra.

rajjamadāsi.meaning_2: found pleasure in dominion; enjoyed kingship
rajjamadāsi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word appears to be a compound of 'rajja' (kingship, dominion) and 'adāsi' (gave, offered). Given the context of 'found pleasure in', it likely means 'enjoyed dominion' or 'found pleasure in kingship'. The 'a' prefix in 'adāsi' could be a vestige of a different construction or indicate a specific nuance of 'giving' or 'offering' oneself to the dominion.

santatimahāmattassa.grammar: masc, comp, gen sg of santatimahāmattā
santatimahāmattassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a genitive singular form indicating possession. The compound 'santatimahāmattā' itself is composed of 'santati' (continuity) and 'mahāmattā' (chief minister). Therefore, the phrase translates to 'of the chief minister of continuity'.

bālajanānaṃ.meaning_2: foolish people; ignorant people; immature people
bālajanānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'bāla' (foolish, ignorant, young) and 'jana' (person, man). Therefore, 'bālajana' refers to people who are foolish, ignorant, or immature.

saṃsīdanaṭṭhānametanti.meaning_2: This is the state of sinking, and so...
saṃsīdanaṭṭhānametanti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. 'saṃsīdana' means sinking, 'aṭṭhāna' means impossibility or wrong place, and 'eta' means this. The verb ending 'ti' indicates 'it is' or 'so'. Therefore, the phrase means 'this is the impossible state of sinking' or 'this is the wrong place for sinking, and so...'

khandhalokādisaṅkhātaṃ.meaning_2: the world of aggregates; the world consisting of the five aggregates (khandhas); the world of sensory experience
khandhalokādisaṅkhātaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'khandha' (aggregate, collection) and 'loka' (world). In Buddhist philosophy, 'khandhaloka' refers to the empirical world as composed of the five aggregates (rupa, vedana, sañña, sankhara, viññana), which are the objects of clinging and the basis of suffering.

sattaratanādivicittaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word refers to the 'seven treasures' which is a compound word formed from 'satta' (seven) and 'ratana' (treasure).

vatthālaṅkārādicittitaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word is a compound. 'vatthu' means cloth, 'alaṅkāra' means ornament, and 'ādi' means etc. 'cittita' is a past participle meaning designed or created. Therefore, the entire word describes something that is adorned with clothes, ornaments, and similar items.

rāgasaṅgādīsu.meaning_2: attachment etc.; and so on; and so forth; lit. beginning with desire and attachment
rāgasaṅgādīsu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound formed from 'rāga' (desire, passion), 'saṅga' (attachment, clinging), and 'ādi' (beginning with, etc.). The '-isu' ending indicates the locative plural, meaning 'in attachments, desires, etc.'. It's used to encompass a range of negative tendencies or states of mind.

sammajjanattheravatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word refers to the act of sweeping, likely in the context of maintaining cleanliness within a monastic setting, as suggested by the presence of 'thera' (elder monk) and 'vaṭṭhu' (matter/case).

sammajjanattheraṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is in the genitive singular case, indicating possession or relation, forming a compound with 'theraṃ'.

mahākusīto.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound adjective formed by combining the prefix 'mahā-' (great, very) with the adjective 'kusīta' (lazy, slack). The context implies an extreme degree of laziness.

nāmetassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a genitive singular form of the pronoun 'ta' (that), combined with 'nāma' (name). In this context, 'nāmetassa' likely refers to 'of that name' or 'its name', implying possession or relation to a previously mentioned name or concept.

ovādamassa.meaning_2: advice; instruction; encouragement; exhortation; order; command
ovādamassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word ovāda, in the context of the provided dictionary entries, can mean either 'advice' or 'command'. Without the actual sentence, it's impossible to determine the precise meaning. The ending 'assa' is likely a pronominal suffix indicating possession or dative case.

ehāvusoti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'āvusoti' is a sandhi compound of 'āvus' (sir/venerable) and 'iti' (thus/and so). It functions adverbially, indicating a conclusion or continuation based on what was previously said, similar to 'and so, sir' or 'thus, venerable one'.

asammajjitvā.meaning_2: not having wiped; not having cleaned; not having swept; not having polished
asammajjitvā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a negative absolutive form. The prefix 'na' negates the action of 'sammajjitvā', which means 'having wiped', 'having cleaned', 'having swept', or 'having polished'. Therefore, 'asammajjitvā' means 'not having performed any of these actions'.

sammajjanatthera.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound of 'sammajjana' (sweeping) and 'thera' (elder monk). The meaning is an elder monk who is engaged in the act of sweeping.

pamādakāle.meaning_2: time of carelessness; period of negligence
pamādakāle.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'pamāda' (carelessness, negligence) and 'kāla' (time). It refers to a time when one is careless or negligent.

idānāmhi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'idān"i' in the text is a compound of 'ima' (this) and 'dāni' (now). It functions as an adverb meaning 'now' or 'at present'.

vattapaṭivattakaraṇena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound noun formed by combining 'vatta' (circle, course, duty) and 'paṭivatta' (reciprocation, return, also duties). The suffix '-karaṇena' indicates the instrumental case, suggesting 'by means of' or 'through'. sajjhāyādīhi.meaning_2: recitation etc.; chanting etc.; rehearsal etc.; repetition etc.

okāsalokaṃ.meaning_2: space of the world; the world's open space
okāsalokaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'okāsa' (space, open space) and 'loka' (world). In this context, it refers to the tangible, physical space of the world, implying the expansiveness and openness of the universe.

aṅgulimālattheravatthu.meaning_2: the story of Aṅgulimāla the elder; the case of Aṅgulimāla the elder
aṅgulimālattheravatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. 'aṅgulimālattheravatthu' is a compound word formed by the sandhi of 'Aṅgulimāla thera' and 'vatthu'.

pesakāradhītāvatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from pesakāra (weaver) and dhītar (daughter). The feminine ending -ā is added to the stem.

jeṭṭhakaniṭṭhā.meaning_2: eldest and youngest; senior and junior
jeṭṭhakaniṭṭhā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound adjective formed from 'jeṭṭhaka' (elder, eldest) and 'kaṇiṭṭha' (younger, youngest). In the context of families or groups, it signifies the senior and junior members.

athekasmiṃ.meaning_2: in one; in a certain; in a single
athekasmiṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound. It is formed from 'atha' (and then; or; after that; because of) and 'ekasmiṃ' (in one; in a certain; in a single, locative singular of 'eka'). The meaning is 'and in one' or 'and in a certain'.

nānābhaṇḍaṃ.meaning_2: various goods; different wares; diverse articles
nānābhaṇḍaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'nānā' (various) and 'bhaṇḍa' (goods, wares, merchandise). In this context, it refers to a variety of items or goods.

pabbajitattā.meaning_2: monk; monastic; renunciant; renunciate; lit. went forth

susānagopikā.meaning_2: female keeper of a cremation ground
susānagopikā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'susāna' (cremation ground) and 'gopikā' (female keeper or attendant). The meaning is derived from the combined meaning of its constituent parts.

dhārāvegena.meaning_2: the force/speed of a stream or flow; the speed of a current
dhārāvegena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound of 'dhārā' (stream, flow) and 'vega' (force, speed, current). It refers to the impetuous flow or rapid movement of water.

bhītaadaṇḍapuriso.meaning_2: a person afraid of the stick; a fearful person
bhītaadaṇḍapuriso.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound formed from 'bhīta' (afraid), 'daṇḍa' (stick/punishment), and 'purisa' (person). The context would determine whether it refers to someone literally afraid of a stick or metaphorically afraid of punishment.

pesakāradhītā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'pesakāra' (weaver, embroiderer) and 'dhītar' (daughter). The suffix '-ā' indicates the feminine nominative singular case. Therefore, 'pesakāradhītā' means 'the weaver's daughter'.

aggāḷavavihāraṃ.meaning_2: Shrine of Aggāḷava; Monastery of Aggāḷava

mahāgotamabuddhoti.meaning_2: the Great Gotama Buddha; the highly venerable Buddha of the Gotama clan

maraṇabhāvaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by combining 'maraṇa' (death) and 'bhāva' (state, condition). In the context of the sentence, it refers to the state or condition of dying.

maraṇajālena.meaning_2: net of death; entanglement of death

anamataggakathaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This adjective describes something that has no discernible or measurable beginning, emphasizing its endlessness or eternality.

tanubhūtasoko.meaning_2: having sorrow diminished; whose sorrow has been reduced
tanubhūtasoko.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound adjective formed from 'tanubhūta' (reduced, diminished) and 'soka' (sorrow). It describes a state where sorrow has been lessened or thinned out.

tiṃsabhikkhuvatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the cardinal number 'thirty', functioning as a quantifier.

haṃsādiccapatheti.meaning_2: the swan of the sun's path is
haṃsādiccapatheti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word appears to be a sandhi compound formed from haṃsa (swan), ādiccapatha (path of the sun), and iti (thus/is).
