sippadassanaṃ.meaning_2: skill; art; craft; branch of knowledge; seeing; sight; insight
sippadassanaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound of 'sippa' (skill, art, craft) and 'dassana' (seeing, sight, vision). The meaning will depend on the specific context of the sentence, but it likely refers to the 'sight' or 'vision' related to a particular skill or art.

naṭaputta.meaning_2: son of a dancer or actor
naṭaputta.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'naṭa' (dancer, actor, performer) and 'putta' (son, child). The word literally means 'son of a dancer' or 'son of an actor'.

hāsayassu.meaning_2: make laugh; please; make happy; delight
hāsayassu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a present tense verb form derived from the causative stem 'hāsaya' (to make laugh). The suffix '-ssu' indicates the second person singular imperative, hence it translates to 'make (you) laugh'.

passitukāmoti.meaning_2: wishing to see; desirous of seeing
passitukāmoti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound adjective formed by the past participle `passita` (seen) and the adjective `kāma` (wishing, desirous). It indicates a state of wanting to see or being eager to see something.

hāsayāmi.meaning_2: may laugh; may joke; may be happy; may rejoice
hāsayāmi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the optative form of the verb 'to laugh' or 'to rejoice'. The ending '-eyya' indicates a potential or subjunctive mood, suggesting a possibility or wish. In the context of the sentence, it would mean 'may one laugh' or 'one might laugh'.

vaṃsamatthakato.meaning_2: the highest point of the lineage; the peak of the family
vaṃsamatthakato.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound formed from 'vaṃsa' (lineage, family) and 'matthaka' (top, head, summit). The suffix '-to' indicates the instrumental case, suggesting 'by the highest point of the lineage' or 'from the peak of the family'.

cuddasakkhattuṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is an adverbial form indicating repetition, specifically 'fourteen times'. It's formed from the cardinal number 'cuddasa' (fourteen) combined with the adverbial suffix '-kkhattuṃ' which signifies 'times' or 'occasions'.

vaṃsamatthakeva.meaning_2: at the top of the lineage; in the lineage itself
vaṃsamatthakeva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'vaṃsa' (lineage), 'matthaka' (top, head), and 'eva' (emphasis). The meaning 'at the top of the lineage' or 'in the lineage itself' is derived from the locative singular form of 'matthaka' combined with 'vaṃsa' and the emphatic particle 'eva'.

ālayādīni.meaning_2: home; roost; perch; nest; lair; attachment (to); clinging (to); craving; reliance; thing relied on; pretence
ālayādīni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'ālaya' in the given context refers to a dwelling place, such as a home or a nest, aligning with its primary meaning. It can also extend to metaphorical meanings like attachment or reliance.

abhiññāpariññāpahānabhāvanāsacchikiriyav.meaning_2: by means of direct knowledge and complete comprehension, abandonment, development, and realization; through the path of insight knowledge, comprehension, abandonment, and realization.
abhiññāpariññāpahānabhāvanāsacchikiriyav.family_compound: abhiññā pariññā pahāna bhāvanā sacchikiriyā vasa
abhiññāpariññāpahānabhāvanāsacchikiriyav.construction: abhiññā + pariññā + pahāna + bhāvanā + sacchikiriyā + vasa + ena
abhiññāpariññāpahānabhāvanāsacchikiriyav.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound formed from several abstract nouns indicating aspects of the path to liberation, followed by the instrumental singular of 'vasa' (power, means) which functions as an adverbial suffix. The entire compound describes the 'way' or 'means' by which these spiritual attainments are achieved.

khandhadhātuāyatanādibhede.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'khandhadhātuāyatanādibhede' is a compound. The first part, 'khandhadhātuāyatana', refers to the aggregates (khandha), elements (dhātu), and sense bases (āyatana). The second part, 'ādi', in this context, functions as an indeclinable meaning 'etc.' or 'and so on'. The final part, 'bhede', means 'in distinctions' or 'in varieties'. Therefore, the entire word signifies 'in the distinctions of aggregates, elements, sense bases, and so on'.

sabbasaṅkhate.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'sabba' (all) and 'saṅkhata' (conditioned, created, fabricated). In this context, it refers to all things that are conditioned or brought into being by causes and conditions, contrasting with the unconditioned (asaṅkhata).

saṭṭhivassikatthero.meaning_2: an elder monk who is sixty years old
saṭṭhivassikatthero.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of three distinct elements: 'saṭṭhi' (sixty), 'vassika' (years old), and 'thera' (elder monk). It clearly denotes a senior monk of sixty years of age.

chinnasaṃyojanā.meaning_2: having cut off fetters; having removed bonds
chinnasaṃyojanā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This compound adjective is formed from 'chinna' (cut off, severed) and 'saṃyojana' (fetter, bond). It describes someone who has successfully overcome or removed spiritual fetters or attachments.

vicaraṇakāraṇaṃ.meaning_2: reason for walking around; reason for roaming; cause for going around
vicaraṇakāraṇaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'vicaraṇa' (walking around, roaming) and 'kāraṇa' (reason, cause). The meaning in context would be the 'reason for the act of walking around' or 'the cause of wandering'.

arahattūpanissayakāraṇanti.meaning_2: the cause/reason for the state of being an arahant
arahattūpanissayakāraṇanti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound formed from 'arahatta', 'upanissaya', and 'kāraṇa'. The first two terms together mean 'the condition or support for becoming an arahant', and 'kāraṇa' means 'cause' or 'reason'. Thus, the entire compound refers to the reason or factor that leads to the attainment of the state of an arahant.

suvaṇṇacetiye.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'suvaṇṇa' (golden) and 'cetiya' (shrine, stupa). The context implies a shrine made of gold or decorated with gold.

cetiyaṭṭhānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'cetiyaṭṭhānaṃ' is a compound word formed from 'cetiya' (shrine) and 'ṭhāna' (place). The '-ṃ' ending indicates the accusative singular neuter, functioning adverbially here, meaning 'at the place of the shrine' or 'in the shrine-location'.

pattamassa.grammar: pron, masc & nt gen sg of ima
pattamassa.meaning_2: his; of him; its; of it
pattamassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a genitive singular form of the demonstrative pronoun 'ima' (this), which agrees in gender with 'assa' (horse).

naṭakārako.meaning_2: actor; performer; stage manager; manager of a theatre; author of a drama
naṭakārako.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'naṭakāraka' is a compound word formed from 'naṭa' (dancer, actor) and 'kāraka' (doer, maker). In this context, it likely refers to someone involved in the production or management of a play or performance, possibly an actor-manager or a theatre director.

naṭagehe.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'naṭa' (dancer, actor) and 'geha' (house). Therefore, 'naṭageha' refers to a house or building associated with dancers or actors, such as a theatre or a dance hall.

khīṇāsavattherassa.meaning_2: who has destroyed the effluents; awakened; epithet of an arahant
khīṇāsavattherassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound adjective formed from 'khīṇa' (destroyed) and 'āsava' (effluents). It is an epithet for an arahant, indicating one who has eradicated all defilements.

dinnapiṇḍapātaṃ.meaning_2: offering of alms-food; lit. given lump-dropping
dinnapiṇḍapātaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'dinna' is a past participle from the root √dā 'to give', meaning 'given'. 'piṇḍapāta' refers to alms-food, literally 'lump dropping'. Together, 'dinnapiṇḍapāta' means 'offering of alms-food' or 'given alms-food'.

naṭadhītā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'naṭa' (dancer/actor) and 'dhītā' (daughter). The meaning is specifically 'dancer's daughter', indicating the profession of her father.

cūḷadhanuggahapaṇḍitavatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This refers to a less accomplished or junior archer, as indicated by 'cūḷa' meaning 'lesser' or 'minor', combined with 'dhanuggaha' meaning 'archer'.

cūḷadhanuggahapaṇḍitaṃ.meaning_2: archer with a lesser bow; lesser archer
cūḷadhanuggahapaṇḍitaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'cūḷadhanuggaha' is a compound word. 'Cūḷa' means 'lesser' or 'smaller', and 'dhanuggaha' means 'archer' (one who holds a bow). Thus, 'cūḷadhanuggaha' refers to an archer who uses a lesser or smaller bow, or it could imply a less skilled or junior archer in comparison to a 'mahādhanuggaha' (great archer).

pattasalākaṃ.meaning_2: a ticket or slip of wood for drawing lots; a lot-stick
pattasalākaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound of 'patta' (bowl) and 'salākā' (stick/ticket). The meaning in context is a stick used for drawing lots, likely for distribution or selection.

salākayāguṃ.meaning_2: a kind of gruel made with stick-like ingredients or for an ailment characterized by stick-like symptoms
salākayāguṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word appears to be a compound of 'salākā' (rod, stick, sliver) and 'yāgu' (gruel, congee). The context in which it is used would clarify whether it refers to a gruel made with ingredients resembling sticks, or a gruel prepared for an illness involving stick-like symptoms or protrusions.

udakatthāya.meaning_2: for the sake of water; for water
udakatthāya.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound formed from 'udaka' (water) and 'attha' (purpose, benefit) in the dative case with the suffix 'āya'. It functions as an adverb meaning 'for the sake of water'.

vicaraṇakamanussameva.meaning_2: walking around for human beings only
vicaraṇakamanussameva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. The word 'vicaraṇakamanussameva' is formed by combining 'vicaraṇakamanussa' and 'eva'. 'vicaraṇakamanussa' itself is a compound of 'vicaraṇa' (walking around), 'manussa' (human being), and 'eva' (only). In this context, it means 'only for human beings who are wandering about'.

kathipāheneva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'kathā' (meaning 'story', 'saying', 'discourse') and 'eva' (an emphatic particle meaning 'even', 'also', 'just'). In this context, 'kathipāheneva' functions as an adverbial phrase meaning 'even when speaking' or 'also when talking'.

uppaṇḍupaṇḍukajātosīti.meaning_2: one who has become extremely pale and jaundiced
uppaṇḍupaṇḍukajātosīti.construction: ud + paṇḍu + paṇḍu + ka + √jan > jā + ta
uppaṇḍupaṇḍukajātosīti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound adjective describing a state of extreme paleness and yellowness, likely due to illness.

avadāpetvā.meaning_1: having made somebody spoken or said
avadāpetvā.meaning_2: having caused to be said; having made tell
avadāpetvā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the absolutive form of the causative verb vadāpeti, indicating an action that has been completed and leads to another action. The context of 'having caused to be said' or 'having made tell' implies that someone was prompted or instructed to speak or narrate something.

aggadhanuggahapaṇḍitaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'Agga' means highest or foremost, and 'dhanuggaha' means archer. Therefore, 'aggadhanuggaha' means the foremost archer, implying a master or the best archer.

taṃmuhuttadiṭṭhake.meaning_2: seen at that moment; discovered at that instant
taṃmuhuttadiṭṭhake.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'taṃ muhutta' (that moment) and 'adiṭṭhaka' (unseen). The construction 'taṃmuhuttadiṭṭhaka' implies something that was not seen or discovered 'at that moment' or 'at that instant'.

cūḷadhanuggahapaṇḍitakāle.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound adjective meaning 'minor archer'. It is formed by combining 'cūḷa' (lesser) and 'dhanuggaha' (archer).

ekūnapaññāsacore.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'ekūnapaññāsa' means forty-nine. It is a compound word formed from 'ekūna' (less by one) and 'paññāsa' (fifty).

diṭṭhacore.meaning_2: thief who has been seen; seen thief
diṭṭhacore.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'diṭṭha' (seen) and 'cora' (thief). It implies a thief who has been spotted or identified.

asitharuṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound of 'asi' (sword) and 'tharu' (weapon-craft or hilt/handle of a weapon). Given the context of weapons, it likely refers to the hilt or handle of a sword.

dhanuggahapaṇḍitassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'dhanu' (bow) and 'gaha' (holding), literally meaning 'one who holds a bow'. In the context of archery, it refers to an archer. The entry also suggests it can mean a teacher of archery.

gamanabhāvañca.meaning_2: going; walking; journeying; travelling; departure; leaving; course; procedure; undertaking; walk; journey; trip
gamanabhāvañca.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'gamanabhāvañca' is a compound word. 'gamana' refers to going or a journey, and 'bhāva' refers to state or nature. 'ca' is a conjunction meaning 'and'. Therefore, 'gamanabhāvañca' likely means 'and the nature of going' or 'and the state of journeying'.

tiṇṇosi.meaning_2: crossed over; gone beyond; delivered; safe
tiṇṇosi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word means 'crossed over' or 'gone beyond'. In a religious or philosophical context, it can also imply being delivered or safe from suffering, having overcome obstacles or the cycle of rebirth.

dānito.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'dānita' is a past participle, derived from the verb 'dāyati' (to give). It signifies something that has been given, bestowed, or offered. The context of the sentence would further specify what was given.

nayīdha.meaning_2: not here; not in this way
nayīdha.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is an indeclinable particle meaning 'not here' or 'not in this way'. It appears to be a combination of the negative 'na' and 'īdha', which is an adverb of place meaning 'here'.

susoṇi.meaning_2: bitch; female dog; hips; waist; buttocks
susoṇi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound of the prefix 'su-' (well, good) and 'soṇī' (bitch, female dog; or hips, waist, buttocks).  Without a sentence, it is difficult to determine the precise meaning. It could mean a 'good bitch' or a 'well-formed hip/waist/buttocks'.

appapaññosi.meaning_2: lacking in wisdom; low in intelligence
appapaññosi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'appapaññosi' is a conjugated form derived from the adjective 'appapañño'. The provided dictionary entry for 'appapañña' indicates it is an adjective meaning 'lacking in wisdom; low in intelligence', literally 'little understanding'. The suffix '-si' attached to the stem 'appapaññ' suggests a second-person singular present tense verb form, implying 'you are lacking in wisdom'.

katañceva.meaning_2: and done; and performed; and made
katañceva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound of the past participle 'kata' (done, performed, made) and the conjunction 'ca' (and). In this context, it functions as a compound conjunction meaning 'and done' or 'and performed', indicating the completion of an action alongside other actions.

punapevaṃ.meaning_2: and so again; and thus again
punapevaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'puna' (again) and 'evaṃ' (thus, so). The combination suggests a continuation of a previous action or state, but with an emphasis on its recurrence. In context, it likely means 'and so again' or 'and thus again', reinforcing a repeated action or situation with a sense of consequence or inevitability.

cūḷadhanuggahapaṇḍito.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound meaning 'a minor archer'. The word 'cūḷa' acts as an adjective meaning 'lesser' or 'minor', modifying 'dhanuggaha' (archer).

siṅgālarūpena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word, siṅgāla, refers to a jackal. It is likely used metaphorically or literally in the text.

niggahakārako.meaning_2: one who restrains or makes restraint; one who refutes or makes refutation
niggahakārako.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'niggaha' (restraint, refutation) and 'kāraka' (doer, maker). The context would determine whether it means one who restrains or one who refutes.

aggapaṇḍitaṃ.meaning_2: wise; intelligent; astute; learned; knowledgeable; skilled
aggapaṇḍitaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'aggapaṇḍitaṃ' is a compound of 'agga' (highest, chief, best) and 'paṇḍita' (wise, learned). In this context, it means 'chiefly wise' or 'extremely wise', indicating a person of supreme wisdom or learning.

bahalarāgassa.meaning_2: intense passion; strong desire; lust; greed
bahalarāgassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'bahala' (intense, strong) and 'rāga' (passion, desire, lust, greed). In the context of the Pāḷi text, it refers to an intense or strong form of passion or desire.

subhanimittagāhādivasena.meaning_2: by means of attractive objects, beautiful mental images, ideas, etc.; as attractive objects, beautiful mental images, ideas, etc.
subhanimittagāhādivasena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. The meaning 'by means of...' is derived from the suffix '-vasena'. The components 'subhanimitta', 'gāha', 'divasa', and 'ādi' refer to attractive objects/mental images, ideas/beliefs, days, and so on, respectively.

vissaṭṭhamānasatāya.grammar: fem, abstr, in comps, from vissaṭṭha, mānasa, tā
vissaṭṭhamānasatāya.meaning_2: the state of having a mind that is loose or lax; the state of having an intention that is loose or lax
vissaṭṭhamānasatāya.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'vissaṭṭha' (loose, lax) and 'mānasatā' (state of mind, intention). The combined meaning refers to a state of mind or intention that is not firm, or is easily swayed. This implies a lack of concentration or resolve.

taṇhābandhanaṃ.meaning_2: bondage of craving; fetters of desire
taṇhābandhanaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'taṇhā' (craving, desire) and 'bandhana' (bond, fetter). In the context of Buddhist teachings, it refers to the suffering and entrapment caused by insatiable desires and attachments. The neuter gender and the '-a' suffix are typical for abstract nouns derived from compounds or roots, and the '-ana' suffix on 'bandhana' indicates an action or state.

suthiraṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by the prefix 'su' (meaning well; easy; right; good; thoroughly) and the adjective 'thira' (meaning firm; solid; stable; reliable). The resulting word 'sutira' therefore means 'very firm' or 'very stable'.

micchāvitakkādīnaṃ.meaning_2: wrong thoughts; incorrect reflections; unwholesome thoughts; evil thoughts
micchāvitakkādīnaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'micchā' (false, wrong) and 'vitakka' (thought, reflection). The plural form 'micchāvitakkādīnaṃ' indicates 'of wrong thoughts and the like', suggesting a category of unwholesome mental states.

vūpasamasaṅkhāte.meaning_2: peace (of); calming (of); subsiding (of); settling (of); appeasement (of); conciliation (of)
vūpasamasaṅkhāte.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'vūpasama' (peace, calming) and 'saṅkhāta' (reckoned, called). In context, it likely refers to a state that is 'called' or 'known' as peace or calming, possibly a cultivated state of mind or a specific teaching related to achieving peace.

asubhajhānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'asubha' (ugly, disgusting) and 'jhāna' (meditation). The meaning is a meditation on the unattractiveness or foulness of things, likely in the context of Buddhist contemplative practice.

rāhulattherassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound meaning Venerable Rāhula. 'thera' here refers to a senior monk, and given that Rāhula was the Buddha's son and became an arahant, it indicates his seniority and respect within the monastic order.

vasavattibhavane.meaning_2: in the state of being master; in the state of having control
vasavattibhavane.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of vasavattī (master, controller) and bhāva (state, existence). It refers to the state of being a master or having control. The '-e' ending indicates the locative case, signifying 'in the state of being master'.

gandhakuṭipamukhe.meaning_2: epithet of the Buddha's dwelling; lit. perfumed hut
gandhakuṭipamukhe.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the first part of the compound word 'gandhakuṭipamukhe'. It refers to the perfumed hut or dwelling of the Buddha.

rujanakaaṅgulī.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound of rujanakā (aching) and aṅgulī (finger or toe). The context would determine whether it refers to an aching finger or toe. The dictionary entries for aṅguli and aṅgulī show that 'finger' and 'toe' are both possible meanings.

mārabhāvaṃ.meaning_2: the state of Mara; existence of Mara; the condition of Mara
mārabhāvaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'māra' (death; Death personified) and 'bhāva' (state; condition; nature). Therefore, 'mārabhāva' refers to the state or existence of Mara, often implying the condition associated with death or temptation.

mahāvīriyo.meaning_2: having great effort; with great energy
mahāvīriyo.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'mahā' (great) and 'vīriya' (effort/energy). The ending '-o' indicates it's in the masculine vocative singular, modifying a masculine noun in that case. It describes someone who possesses great effort or energy.

rāgasantāsādīnaṃ.meaning_2: of desires and terrors and so forth
rāgasantāsādīnaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound meaning 'of desires, terrors, and so forth'. The ending '-aṃ' indicates the genitive plural.

asantasanako.meaning_1: one who causes fear or terror
asantasanako.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word appears to be a masculine noun derived from the root √tas (to be terrified, to be scared) compounded with the prefix saṃ (intensive) and the suffix aka (agentive suffix). The meaning 'one who causes fear' or 'terrifying' fits the context where a fearful entity or being is being described.

sannipātasaṅkhātaṃ.meaning_2: which is called a sannipāta (assembly, congregation, union; or illness produced by combination of the three humours)
sannipātasaṅkhātaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound of 'sannipāta' and 'saṅkhāta'. Based on the dictionary entries, 'sannipāta' can refer to an assembly, congregation, or union of things. It can also specifically refer to a serious illness caused by the combination of the three humours in Ayurveda. 'Saṅkhāta' means 'reckoned', 'so called', or 'named'. Therefore, 'sannipātasaṅkhāta' means 'what is called a sannipāta'.

akkharapiṇḍañca.meaning_2: letter of the alphabet; syllable; morpheme
akkharapiṇḍañca.construction: na > a + √khar + a + piṇḍa + a + ca
akkharapiṇḍañca.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'akkhara' (letter/syllable) and 'piṇḍa' (lump/ball) with the conjunction 'ca' (and). In this context, it likely refers to a collection or mass of letters or syllables.

pubbakkharena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'pubba' (previous) and 'akkhara' (letter or syllable). In this context, it refers to the preceding letter or syllable within a word.

aparakkharaṃ.meaning_2: having no following letter; not the next syllable
aparakkharaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound, formed by the negative prefix 'na' (not) and 'parākkharā' (following letter/syllable). In the context of the sentence, it signifies something that is not the subsequent letter or syllable.

aparakkharena.meaning_2: not next; not preceding; not following
aparakkharena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a negative compound, formed by the negative prefix 'na' and the word 'parakkhara' which means 'next letter' or 'next syllable'. Therefore, 'aparakkhara' means 'not the next letter' or 'not the following syllable'.

pubbakkharañca.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'pubba' (previous, earlier) and 'akkhara' (letter, syllable, word). In this context, it likely refers to a preceding letter or sound within a word or sequence.

majjhapariyosānesu.meaning_2: ending in the middle; culminating in the middle
majjhapariyosānesu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'majjha' (middle) and 'pariyosāna' (end, finish, conclusion). In this context, it likely refers to something that concludes or ends in the middle, suggesting a partial or intermediate stage.

pubbakkharaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'pubba' (previous, earlier) and 'akkhara' (letter, syllable). The construction indicates it's a direct combination without complex sandhi rules. The meaning 'initial letter' fits perfectly in a grammatical context where the first letter of a word or concept is being discussed.

ādimajjhesu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound adjective formed from 'ādi' (first, initial) and 'majjha' (middle). It describes something that pertains to both the beginning and the middle.

ṭhitasarīro.meaning_2: with a body; having a body
ṭhitasarīro.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is part of a compound word 'ṭhitasarīro'. The meaning of 'sarīra' here is 'body'. Combined with 'ṭhita', it suggests 'having a stable or firm body'.

atthadhammaniruttipaṭibhānānaṃ.meaning_2: the understanding of meaning, doctrine, grammar and wit
atthadhammaniruttipaṭibhānānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from four nouns: 'attha' (meaning), 'dhamma' (doctrine, reality), 'nirutti' (grammar, interpretation), and 'paṭibhāna' (wit, eloquence, intuition). The meaning is the understanding of these four aspects.

sīlakkhandhādīnañca.meaning_2: and the aggregates of virtue etc.; and the categories of virtue etc.
sīlakkhandhādīnañca.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound. 'sīlakkhandha' refers to 'aggregates/categories of virtue'. 'ādi' means 'etc.' or 'beginning with'. 'na' is a genitive ending indicating possession or relationship, and 'ca' means 'and'. The entire compound implies 'and the aggregates/categories of virtue and so forth'.

vimuttacittatāya.grammar: fem, abstr, in comps, from vimuttacitta
vimuttacittatāya.meaning_2: the state of having a liberated mind; the state of having an emancipated heart
vimuttacittatāya.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound formed from 'vimuttacitta' (with a liberated mind) and the abstractive suffix 'tā' (state of being). It refers to the condition or quality of having a liberated mind.

upakājīvakavatthu.meaning_1: the case of Upaka the ascetic
upakājīvakavatthu.meaning_2: case of Upaka the ascetic; the narrative concerning Upaka the ascetic
upakājīvakavatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound, referring to a specific incident or 'case' involving Upaka the ascetic. The related dictionary entries show 'jīvakavatthu' meaning 'case of Jīvaka', and 'upaka' as a name for an ascetic. Therefore, 'upakājīvakavatthu' likely refers to a narrative or discussion pertaining to Upaka the ascetic.

pattasabbaññutaññāṇo.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound. The first part, 'patta', likely derives from the past participle of 'pāpuṇāti' (to reach, attain), meaning 'attained' or 'reached'. The second part, 'sabbaññutā', means 'omniscience'. The third part, 'ñāṇo', means 'knowledge'. Therefore, the entire word signifies 'one who has attained the knowledge of omniscience'.

dhammacakkapavattanatthaṃ.meaning_2: for the sake of the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma; for the purpose of setting the Dhamma-wheel in motion
dhammacakkapavattanatthaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'Dhammacakka' means 'wheel of Dhamma' or 'Dhamma teaching'. 'Pavattana' means 'turning' or 'setting in motion'. The suffix '-atthaṃ' (accusative singular of 'attha') indicates 'for the sake of' or 'for the purpose of'. Therefore, the entire word translates to 'for the sake of the turning of the Wheel of Dhamma', referring to the Buddha's first sermon.

aṭṭhārasayojanamaggaṃ.meaning_2: eighteen yojanas (approximately 360 km); a great distance
aṭṭhārasayojanamaggaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'aṭṭhārasa' (eighteen) and 'yojana' (a unit of distance, approximately 20 km). The resulting compound acts as an adjective describing a great distance.

tebhūmakadhammānaṃ.meaning_2: teaching of the three realms; doctrine of the three worlds
tebhūmakadhammānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound formed from 'tebhūmaka' (three-tiered; three-storied; triple-layered) and 'dhamma' (teaching; discourse; doctrine). It specifically refers to the Buddhist doctrine pertaining to the three realms of existence (sense-sphere, form-sphere, and formless-sphere).

viditasabbacatubhūmakadhammo.meaning_2: the doctrine/teaching known to all, having four stages
viditasabbacatubhūmakadhammo.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. 'vidita' means known or understood. 'sabba' means all. 'catubhūmaka' means having four storeys or stages. 'dhamma' can mean doctrine, teaching, or truth. In this context, it likely refers to the doctrine or teaching that is known to all and has four stages or levels of understanding.

tebhūmakadhammesu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'tebhūmaka' (three-tiered) and 'dhamma' (doctrine or teaching). In this context, it refers to a doctrine that spans three realms or levels, likely referring to the three planes of existence in Buddhist cosmology (kāmaloka, rūpaloka, arūpaloka).

tebhūmakadhamme.meaning_2: doctrine pertaining to the three realms of existence
tebhūmakadhamme.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'tebhūmaka' (three-tiered) and 'dhamma' (doctrine). The combined meaning refers to Buddhist doctrines that relate to the three realms of existence (sensual, form, and formless).

taṇhakkhayante.meaning_2: wearing away of craving; depletion of desire; extinction of longing
taṇhakkhayante.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'taṇhakkhaya' refers to the cessation or destruction of craving, a core concept in Buddhist philosophy representing the ultimate goal of liberation from suffering.

taṇhakkhayasaṅkhāte.meaning_2: wearing away of craving; depletion of desire; extinction of longing
taṇhakkhayasaṅkhāte.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'taṇhā' (craving) and 'khaya' (wearing away, depletion). It refers to the state of having extinguished craving, a key concept in Buddhist soteriology.

abhiññeyyādibhede.meaning_2: should be understood; should be taken; should be interpreted; lit. to be completely known
abhiññeyyādibhede.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a potential participle derived from the verb 'abhijānāti' (to know completely or to understand thoroughly). In this context, it signifies something that ought to be completely known or understood.

nevābhinandi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by the negative particle 'neva' (not) and the present participle 'abhinandi' (rejoicing, delighting). It describes someone who does not find joy or pleasure in something.

luddakanivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ.meaning_2: hunting place of a hunter; lair of a hunter
luddakanivāsanaṭṭhānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'luddaka' means hunter, 'nivāsa' means dwelling or residence, and 'ṭhāna' means place. Together, it refers to the place where a hunter resides or hunts.

sakkapañhavatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound. 'sakkapañha' refers to 'Sakka's questions' (from DN21 Sakkapañhasutta), and 'vatthu' in this context means 'case' or 'subject matter'. Therefore, 'sakkapañhavatthu' refers to the 'case' or 'subject matter' of the questions asked by Sakka.

cakkavāḷasahassesu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'cakkavāḷa' refers to a world system or a solar system. In the given text, it is used in conjunction with 'sahassesu' meaning 'in thousands', to describe a vast extent of world systems.

mahādevatāsannipātoti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word is a compound of 'mahā' (great) and 'devatāsannipāta' (assembly of deities). This suggests a significant gathering of divine beings.

dānarasaratīsu.meaning_2: does not taste; does not enjoy; does not delight in
dānarasaratīsu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a negative present tense verb form. 'dāna' means gift, and 'rasa' means taste or enjoyment. The negative prefix 'na' is combined with 'dāna' and 'rasa' to form a compound verb. The context of the sentence would clarify what is not being tasted or enjoyed.

dānarasaratī.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'Dāna' means giving, 'rasa' means taste or essence, and 'ratī' means delight or pleasure. In this context, it refers to the delight derived from the act of giving or generosity.

janasahassena.meaning_2: one thousand men; population of a thousand people
janasahassena.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'janasahassena' is a sandhi compound of 'jana' (person, man) and 'sahassa' (thousand). It functions as a masculine noun in the instrumental case, indicating 'by/with a thousand people'.

devasannipātoti.meaning_2: a confluence or gathering of deities; a divine assembly; a collective term for celestial beings
devasannipātoti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'deva' (deity, god) and 'sannipāta' (gathering, assembly). The addition of 'iti' at the end of the word in the text likely functions as a quotative or concluding particle, indicating 'thus' or 'so it is said'. In this context, 'devasannipātoti' would mean '... thus it is called a deva-sannipāta', or '... and so on, referring to a divine assembly.'

kaṅkhacchedanatthameva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a feminine abstract noun derived from the root √kaṅkh, meaning doubt or uncertainty. In the context of 'kaṅkhacchedanatthameva', it signifies the doubt that is to be cut off or destroyed.

pucchitapañhesu.meaning_2: one who has asked a question; one who has been asked a question
pucchitapañhesu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'pucchita' (asked) and 'pañha' (question). It can be interpreted in two ways: either as someone who has asked a question, or someone who has been asked a question, depending on the context of the sentence it appears in. In the context of 'pucchitapañhesu', it likely refers to those who have been asked questions.

seṭṭhoyevāti.meaning_2: foremost (among); best (of); primary; most important; supreme (among)
seṭṭhoyevāti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word seṭṭhoyevāti is a compound formed from 'seṭṭha' (best, foremost) and 'eva' (indeed, certainly) and 'iti' (thus). In this context, it means 'certainly the best' or 'indeed foremost'.

kadaligabbhasadisāni.meaning_2: resembling the womb of a banana plantain tree
kadaligabbhasadisāni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. The word is in the neuter plural accusative case, indicated by the '-āni' ending, used here to describe something that resembles the womb of a banana plantain tree in the context of a sentence. The components are 'kadali' (banana tree), 'gabbha' (womb), and 'sadisa' (similar to).

katānumodanāva.grammar: fem, abstr, act, from kata + anumodanā
katānumodanāva.meaning_2: appreciation of what has been done; thanksgiving for what has been done; rejoicing in merit that has been done
katānumodanāva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound formed by 'kata' (done) and 'anumodanā' (appreciation, thanksgiving). In the context of the given sentence, it signifies the act of appreciating or rejoicing in something that has been completed or done.

paṇītapiṇḍapātassa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'paṇīta' (excellent, delicious) and 'piṇḍapāta' (alms food). Thus, it specifically refers to excellent or delicious food received as alms.

sappitelādīnaṃ.meaning_2: afflicted by ghee and oil; misery of ghee and oil
sappitelādīnaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. The word 'sappiteladina' means 'afflicted by ghee and oil'. It is composed of 'sappi' (ghee), 'tela' (oil), and 'ādīna' (affliction, misery).

dinnabhesajjadānatopi.meaning_2: medicine given as a gift; the gift of medicine
dinnabhesajjadānatopi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'dinna' (given), 'bhesajja' (medicine), and 'dāna' (gift). The word refers to the act or instance of giving medicine as a charitable offering.

mahāvihārasadisānaṃ.meaning_2: great monastery; the Great Monastery in Anurādhapura
mahāvihārasadisānaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the genitive plural form of 'mahāvihāra', meaning 'of great monasteries' or 'of the Great Monastery'. It modifies 'sadisānaṃ'.

lohapāsādasadisānañca.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This refers to the 'Copper Palace' in Anuradhapura, known for its copper tiles. The compound form indicates it's being used as a specific entity or place.

dinnasenāsanadānatopi.meaning_2: from the gift of housing; from the gift of lodging; from the gift of furniture
dinnasenāsanadānatopi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound formed from 'dinna' (given), 'senāsana' (housing, lodging, furniture), and 'dāna' (gift, offering), with the locative singular ending '-to'. The locative ending indicates 'from' or 'in', so the phrase translates to 'from the gift of housing/lodging/furniture'.

katapariccāgatopi.meaning_2: one who has renounced or abandoned; one who has made a sacrifice
katapariccāgatopi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed from 'kata' (done, made) and 'pariccāga' (giving up, sacrifice). It means someone who has completed a sacrifice or abandonment. The suffix '-opi' attached to it is likely an emphatic particle or a conjunction.

anumodanāvasenāpi.meaning_2: due to the transference of merit; by means of the transference of merit
anumodanāvasenāpi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound of 'anumodanā' (transference of merit) and 'vasena' (due to, by means of), indicating that the action is performed because of or through the transference of merit.

uḷuṅkamattaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. 'uḷuṅka' means 'ladle' and 'mattaṃ' is a neuter form of 'matta' which indicates measure or extent. Therefore, 'uḷuṅkamattaṃ' means 'as much as a ladle' or 'the measure of a ladle'.

sakalakappaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'sakalakappaṃ' is a compound. The first part 'sakalakappa' is formed by combining 'sakala' (meaning 'whole', 'entire') with 'kappa' (meaning 'aeon', 'age', 'lifespan of a world system'). In this context, it describes a duration of time that is the 'whole aeon' or 'entire age'.

sāriputtādayopi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of the name of the arahant monk Sāriputta and the word 'ādi' meaning 'etc.' or 'and so on'. It is used here to indicate that Sāriputta and others like him are being referred to.

assajittherādīhi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'assa' (horse) and 'ji' (conqueror), literally meaning 'horse master', but it is used here as the name of a monk. The compound 'therādīhi' indicates that Assaji is being referred to along with other senior monks. The suffix '-īhi' is a plural instrumental ending.

kathitadhammaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'kathitadhammaṃ' is a compound of 'kathita' (said, spoken) and 'dhamma' (teaching, doctrine). In this context, it refers to the 'Dhamma that has been spoken' or the 'expounded teaching'. The 'ṃ' at the end indicates the accusative singular masculine/neuter form, functioning as the object of an implied verb or as a standalone noun phrase.

sāvakapāramīñāṇaṃ.meaning_2: insight into the perfection of discipleship; understanding of the fulfilment of discipleship
sāvakapāramīñāṇaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word is a compound of 'sāvaka pāramī' (fulfilment of discipleship) and 'ñāṇa' (knowing, understanding, insight). The '-ṃ' ending indicates it's in the accusative case, likely functioning as the object of a verb, or in a context implying acquisition of this knowledge.

gandharasādayopi.meaning_2: pleasant taste of smells; pleasing aromas
gandharasādayopi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This compound, 'gandharasa', is formed by combining 'gandha' (smell/fragrance) and 'rasa' (taste/essence). In this context, it refers to the 'pleasant taste of smells' or 'pleasing aromas', suggesting a sensory experience where scent is perceived with a pleasant quality akin to taste.

sudhābhojanarasopi.meaning_2: even the taste of ambrosia food
sudhābhojanarasopi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. It combines 'sudhā' (ambrosia), 'bhojana' (food), 'rasa' (taste), and the indeclinable 'api' (even/also). The meaning is 'even the taste of ambrosia food'.

sattatiṃsabodhipakkhiyadhammasaṅkhāto.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word functions as a cardinal number modifying the subsequent compound noun 'bodhipakkhiyadhammasaṅkhāto'.

navalokuttaradhammasaṅkhāto.meaning_2: called the supramundane states of the nine (or new); defined as supramundane states
navalokuttaradhammasaṅkhāto.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. The primary interpretation of 'nava' here is 'nine', referring to the nine supramundane states (navalokuttaradhamma). However, 'nava' also means 'new', so it could also refer to 'new supramundane states' or 'supramundane states of the new'. Given the context of Buddhist teachings, the interpretation of 'nine supramundane states' is the most common and contextually appropriate. 'Saṅkhāta' here means 'called' or 'defined'.

puttaratidhīturatidhanaratiitthiratinacc.meaning_2: various kinds of pleasures, such as those from sons, daughters, wealth, women, dancing and singing, instrumental music, and so on
puttaratidhīturatidhanaratiitthiratinacc.family_compound: putta rati dhītar rati dhana rati itthi rati nacca gīta vādita ādi rati pabheda
puttaratidhīturatidhanaratiitthiratinacc.construction: putta + rati + dhītar + rati + dhana + rati + itthi + rati + nacca + gīta + vādita + ādi + rati + pabhedā
puttaratidhīturatidhanaratiitthiratinacc.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a very long sandhi compound describing various forms of enjoyment or attachment. It is a list of different types of pleasures, each followed by 'rati' (enjoyment/delight). The final part 'ādiratipabhedā' signifies that these are just examples and there are many other types of pleasures.

anekappabhedā.meaning_2: of many kinds; of various sorts
anekappabhedā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound adjective formed from 'aneka' (many) and 'pabheda' (division, variety). It describes something as being of many different kinds or types.

udaggabhāvaṃ.meaning_2: exalted state; elated state; lofty state
udaggabhāvaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This compound combines 'udagga' (high, lofty, elated) with 'bhāva' (state, condition). Therefore, 'udaggabhāva' signifies a state of being high, lofty, or elated, depending on the specific context of its usage. The provided related entries for 'udagga' offer both literal ('high; lofty; towering') and figurative ('joyful; elated; enraptured') meanings, which can both contribute to the understanding of 'udaggabhāva'.

arahattapariyosānā.meaning_2: awakened state; enlightenment; lit. worthy state
arahattapariyosānā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'arahattapariyosānā' is a compound. The first part, 'arahatta', refers to the state of being an arahat, which signifies spiritual awakening or enlightenment.

sabbaseṭṭhameva.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word 'sabbaseṭṭhamev' is a sandhi compound of 'sabba', 'seṭṭha', and 'eva'. 'Sabba' here functions as an adjective meaning 'all'. The context would determine if it modifies a masculine, neuter, or feminine noun. Based on the provided lemmas, 'sabba' has multiple meanings related to 'all', 'everything', and 'whole', but in this context, 'all' is the most fitting, especially when combined with 'seṭṭha' (best).

evaṃjeṭṭhake.meaning_2: thus foremost; chief in this way
evaṃjeṭṭhake.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. The word 'evaṃjeṭṭhake' combines 'evaṃ' (thus, in this way) and 'jeṭṭhaka' (foremost, chief). The meaning is 'foremost in this way' or 'chiefly in this manner', indicating that something is the most prominent or important according to the preceding description or manner.

ajjādiṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word appears to be a sandhi compound, likely formed from 'ima' and 'ajja'. The provided dictionary entries support 'ajja' as meaning 'today' or 'now', and 'ima' is a demonstrative pronoun. Therefore, 'ajjā' functions as an adverb meaning 'today' or 'now'.

mahādhammassavanaṃ.meaning_2: great listening to the Dhamma; great sermon
mahādhammassavanaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound of 'mahā' (great) and 'dhammassavana' (listening to the Dhamma/sermon). The context would clarify if it refers to a particularly significant or lengthy sermon, or a great act of listening.

pākatikadhammassavanaṃ.meaning_2: listening to the ordinary teaching; listening to a common sermon; listening to the common Dhamma
pākatikadhammassavanaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'pākatika' (ordinary, common) and 'dhammassavana' (hearing the Dhamma). The word implies listening to a sermon or teaching that is regular or not extraordinary.

aputtakaseṭṭhivatthu.meaning_2: property of a childless wealthy man
aputtakaseṭṭhivatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. The first part 'aputtaka' means childless. The second part 'seṭṭhi' refers to a wealthy man or banker. The third part 'vatthu' means property or land. Therefore, the compound refers to the property of a childless wealthy man.

aputtakaseṭṭhiṃ.meaning_2: a wealthy man without a son; a childless banker
aputtakaseṭṭhiṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'aputtaka' (childless) and 'seṭṭhi' (wealthy man, banker). The combined meaning refers to a wealthy individual who lacks an heir.

abhiharāpetvā.meaning_2: to carry to; to bring to; to offer; to present
abhiharāpetvā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the present tense, 3rd person singular form of the verb 'abhiharati'. In the context of the sentence, it likely means 'brings' or 'presents', referring to something being carried or offered.

nānaggarasabhojane.meaning_2: in various cities; in different towns; with diverse foods
nānaggarasabhojane.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] The word appears to be a sandhi compound. 'nāna' means various, 'nara' means people or men, and 'sabhojana' can mean with food or with luxuries. In the context of the sentence, it is likely referring to the variety of food available in different cities or for different groups of people, thus 'in various cities; in different towns; with diverse foods' seems the most fitting translation. Alternatively, it could imply 'for various people in different cities' or 'with various luxuries in different cities'.

vatthayānachattesupi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound where multiple nouns and an indeclinable are joined together. The locative plural ending '-su' is attached to the final component 'api', which is a common occurrence in Pali grammar.

paṇītapiṇḍapātaṃ.meaning_2: excellent alms food; fine lump dropping
paṇītapiṇḍapātaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This compound word combines 'paṇīta' (excellent, fine) with 'piṇḍapāta' (alms food). The combined meaning is 'excellent alms food', emphasizing the high quality of the alms received.

goṇotiādīni.meaning_2: etc.; and so forth; and so on
goṇotiādīni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound of goṇa, iti, and ādi. The meaning is 'etc.' or 'and so on', indicating that the list mentioned before is not exhaustive.

tāvesa.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is the adjectival form of 'tāvasī' (ascetic), implying 'belonging to an ascetic' or 'ascetic-like'.

vuḍḍhippattakāle.meaning_2: the time of attaining increase or prosperity; the time of development
vuḍḍhippattakāle.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'Vuḍḍhi' means increase or prosperity. 'Appatta' means not reached or attained. 'Kāla' means time. Therefore, 'vuḍḍhippattakāla' refers to the time when increase or prosperity has been attained.

gacchamūle.meaning_2: originating from the base of the trees
gacchamūle.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound adjective formed from 'gaccha' (tree) and 'mūla' (root, base). In this context, it describes something originating from the base of the trees.

dummedhapuggalā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word formed by 'dummedha' (foolish, stupid) and 'puggala' (person, individual). The plural form 'dummedhapuggalā' refers to multiple foolish or stupid individuals.

uppannataṇhā.meaning_2: arisen; appeared; come into being (in); born (in)
uppannataṇhā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a past participle meaning 'arisen' or 'born'. It is combined with 'taṇha' (craving) to describe a craving that has arisen.

nibbānapāragavesino.meaning_2: seeking the far shore of Nibbāna; seeking salvation; who is looking for the beyond
nibbānapāragavesino.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of three elements: 'nibbāna' (Nibbāna), 'pāra' (far shore), and 'gavesī' (seeker). The meaning 'seeking the far shore of Nibbāna' is a literal interpretation of the components. The other meanings 'seeking salvation' and 'who is looking for the beyond' are interpretative, reflecting the Buddhist concept of Nibbāna as the ultimate goal.

aṅkuravatthu.meaning_2: the case of the shoot; the story of the shoot
aṅkuravatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. 'aṅkura' means 'shoot' or 'sprout', and 'vatthu' in this context refers to a 'case' or 'story'. Therefore, 'aṅkuravatthu' likely refers to a narrative or case study concerning a shoot or sprout.

kaṭacchumattakaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound adjective meaning 'spoonful'. It is formed by combining 'kaṭacchu' (spoon) with 'mattaka' (size of, amount of). The context would determine if it's referring to the size of a spoonful or a quantity equal to a spoonful.

suvuttabījaṃ.meaning_2: seed of what is well said
suvuttabījaṃ.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a compound word. 'su' is a prefix meaning 'well'. 'vutta' is the past participle of 'vacati' meaning 'said'. 'bīja' means 'seed'. Therefore, 'suvuttabīja' means 'seed of what is well said' or 'seed of good speech'.

yathāsukhetteti.meaning_2: as one likes the field; as the field is fertile according to one's pleasure
yathāsukhetteti.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'yathā' (as), 'sukha' (comfort, pleasure, fertile), 'khetta' (field), and 'iti' (thus, and so). It seems to describe a state or action done according to one's pleasure regarding a fertile field, or perhaps the state of a fertile field itself that is pleasing.

sāmākādīni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound where 'sāmāka' (millet) is combined with 'ādi' (and the like, etc.). The suffix 'ni' indicates a neuter plural accusative or nominative. Since 'sāmākādi' can be used both as an adjective and a noun, and 'ādi' itself can be a noun, the compound likely functions as a noun here, referring to 'millet and other things of that sort'.

pubbaṇṇāparaṇṇāni.meaning_2: primary grains and secondary crops; lit. first grain and other food
pubbaṇṇāparaṇṇāni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound of 'pubbaṇṇāni' and 'aparaṇṇāni'. The 'ā' is inserted due to sandhi rules. The plural form 'āni' indicates these are types of food or crops collectively.

bahuphalāni.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a neuter plural form, referring to multiple 'many fruits' or 'manifold results', depending on the specific context in which it appears. The '-ni' ending is the neuter plural nominative/accusative marker. The compound 'bahuphala' combines 'bahu' (many) with 'phala' (fruit or result).

sesagāthāsupi.meaning_2: even in the remaining verses; also in the remaining verses
sesagāthāsupi.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a sandhi compound. 'sesagāthāsupi' is composed of 'sesagāthā' (remaining verses) and 'api' (even, also). The 'su' is a locative plural ending for feminine nouns like 'gāthā'. Therefore, the word means 'even in the remaining verses' or 'also in the remaining verses'.

taṇhāvaggavaṇṇanā.meaning_2: commentary on the chapter of craving; exegesis of the chapter of craving
taṇhāvaggavaṇṇanā.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'taṇhāvagga' (Chapter 24 of the Dhammapada) and 'vaṇṇanā' (commentary). It refers to the commentary specifically on Chapter 24, which deals with craving.

pañcabhikkhuvatthu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This is a sandhi compound. The primary meaning of vatthu in this context, as indicated by the 'vinaya' classification in the provided dictionary entries, is 'case of...'. Therefore, pañcabhikkhuvatthu refers to a specific legal or disciplinary case involving five monks.

cakkhudvārādīsu.meaning_2: eye door; visual channel; sense door of sight
cakkhudvārādīsu.comment: [gemini: gemini-2.5-flash-lite] This word is a compound of 'cakkhu' (eye) and 'dvara' (door, gate). In the context of the senses, it refers to the visual channel or the sense door of sight. The suffix '-su' indicates a locative plural, implying 'in the eye doors and the like'.

nāgānamanuggahaṃ.meaning_2: support of the noble ones; assistance of great men; help of arahants
nāgānamanuggahaṃ.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] This is a sandhi compound formed from 'nāgānaṃ' (genitive plural of nāga meaning 'of the noble ones/great men') and 'anuggahaṃ' (accusative singular of anuggaha meaning 'support/assistance'). In Buddhist context, this refers to the support or guidance provided by enlightened beings or arahants.

pariyosānenattho.comment: [openrouter: deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3.1:free] The compound 'pariyosānenattho' appears to be a sandhi form of 'pariyosāna + anattha' meaning 'end/conclusion of harm' or 'culmination of misfortune'.
